Dragon’s Dogma: Dark Arisen is an action role playing game, developed by Capcom. The original game was released on PS3 and Xbox 360 in 2013, before the game was finally ported to PC in January 2016.   The game starts with your character being super overpowered, with really rare equipment and dealing tons of damage, giving you a sneak peak into the type of end game content you have to come. But yes, you do get nerfed back down to the regular level 1 RPG character, in your rags and sticks for swords. You are able to choose between a number of different classes, or vocations as they are called in DD. On top of being in control of your character, you will also gain a party of up to three more “pawns”, these too take on specific roles in the group, such as tanks, damage and healers. I found this to be a really nice addition to the game as I wasn’t expecting such mechanics from an RPG game like this. The party controls and management system is basic at best, but the AI is fairly in tune with what they should be doing, and the two basic controls, attack and follow, are both really responsive as well.   The combat system in DD against the smaller style of enemies is very generic hack and slash, there is no real special combos or special abilities to come across, The warrior class is probably the most basic class to play, but is probably the one I would recommend for your first play through.  Where DD’s combat system really comes into its own, is when you get to scale larger enemies, such as giants, and cyclops.  This allows you to climb onto enemies backs and swing at them to deal more damage. This is a feature that I haven’t really seen incorporated into combat systems in recent memory, the last time I remember coming across it is in Shadow of the Colossus.     You can definitely tell this game was ported from the consoles as the graphics are average at best. The game is pretty poorly optimized as even though the graphics didn’t look brilliant, I wasn’t able to get the full 4k effect. The character models look pretty good once you get some more interesting looking armour and weapons to equip. Animation across the game is of a high standard though, with the regular combat hack and slash animations looking very cool when you can couple a few attacks together. You can get some really nice visual effects through the draw distance of the PC version of the game being superior, with some really nice looking environments when you are out in the open world.  This is a game which is completely voice acted, all to a really high standard as well.   DD is a pretty hard game, even on the lower difficulty throughs, you will have challenges. You can really run into high level enemies without realizing it’s too late and your attacks do no damage at all. You have to make use of the game’s block system and your excessively large jump range too in order to dodge attacks and swipes. The use of the pawn system really aids the inexperienced players though, as they scale with your level too.  Whilst DD has a really large open world for you to explore, it is really tedious to travel to and from places. The lack of any staple fast travel system without having to use consumables is a real pain. There was nothing more demoralizing than getting a quest, then seeing it was at the completely opposite side of the map, only to get there, and they tell you to go straight back. This problem at times almost made me not want to continue. There is a fast travel system, but it is not easily accessible and you require items which are not very common to find in the game too.   Completing the game took me twenty hours. I will admit, I didn’t complete as many side quests as I would normally, and this was purely down to the giant map, and no fast travel system. The side quest system is also pretty in-depth too; because if you go too far in the main story line, you are unable to complete some side quests, which means if you want to go for the complentionists approach to this game, you best get that Wiki bookmarked to make sure you don’t miss out on anything! I would say there is an element of replay ability, not only does the game have a New game+ mode, but also has a speed run mode which is nice to see. You could also get another play through out of playing as a different class to change up the variety a bit.   Technically, the game is sound. I didn’t have any crashes or bugs. The graphic side of the game is poorly optimized as my rig should be able to cope with his game on ultra-settings but sadly it got some chugging and frame drops on the higher graphical options. You can tell the game is a console port as the menus are clearly made for consoles, and do not incorporate the use of keyboard and mouse very easily. That being said, I did play the game completely with a keyboard and mouse but the game could quite easily be played using a controller.   In summary, Dragon’s Dogma: Dark Arisen is a really good action RPG game. The only negatives I found are the poorer graphics, and the annoying fast travel system. If these aren’t problems which will grind on you, then DD is a stellar game. The combat system is really interesting, along with an intriguing story line. If you manage to complete all of the side quests on offer, you could easily get 30 or so hours out of this game, plus any further runs you do in the other game modes. The game is really nicely priced at £23,99. I am going with a highly recommendation of this game  [b][u] Tom's Score Card[/u][/b] 1) Stay away 2) Not Recommended 3) Only recommended when on sale 4) Recommended [b][u]5) Highly recommended[/u][/b] 6) This is a must play  If you found this review helpful, please give it a thumbs up. TLDR absolutely very good game.....with mods. Without mods I wouldn't have finished it.   Game is about you as the hero building your kingdom. Very good game, lots of class variety, good story, lots of mini campaigns. Tons of cool items, lots of monsters to kill, lots of role playing decisions. So basically it has all the things you need to make a good game, no complaints here. Some combats are gimmicky, and the game absolutely cheats some mechanics to make things difficult. The kingdom events and how the advisors work aren't well explained so on my first playthrough the kingdom actually failed. I made it easier by adding a mod on the next playthrough. I hear a lot of people don't care for the kingdom mechanics and you can make it automatic if you wish.   I'm not a D&D\pathfinder guy. I've played some video games but never the pen and paper variety. Knowing how things work helps IMMENSELY. The game is not very good at telling you what different buffs do what, what buff stacks with what, what debuffs do, and what counters spells and effects - but it almost always follows the rules from the pen and paper game, which means you have a lot of reference material online if you want to go looking for it. It's easy to get lost with all the spells available and not understand what you need to beat certain things. I always had the Pathfinder reference site D20PFSRD open in a tab because you really need the information at hand.   The game is best played in turn based mode for any combat that might be tricky. The best way to get this is from a mod. You can use this to turn on and off turned base mode with a hotkey, which is awesome since a lot of mid game combat is basically just automatic.   Since there are so many classes and you're going to screw your builds up or just want to try things out, you'll want the respec mod. While the game does allow for respec, it's only at certain locations, and the cost escalates with every time you use it. With the mod it's cheap and you can use it anywhere. Quality of life 10\10. This is also the only way to get the default companions to do a complete respec. If you use the in game respec mechanic, the companions will always have base levels in whatever class the game made them for role playing purposes. I say to heck with that and use the mod so you can make them whatever you want.   There's a ton of classes that aren't included in the game. Add with a mod. You can get more portraits as well with several mods. You can highlight scrolls your character can learn with a mod. And on and on. Head over to Nexus and go wild. Not sure why there's no Steam workshop for this game, but adding mods isn't terrbily hard.   While I did play nearly the entire way through the game with only the turn based mod, with the additional mods I had a lot more fun on the subsequent playthrough. Variety of classes, skills and items and being able to switch things around to try new things out is one of the big things I enjoy about RPG games, so I highly recommend adding a few mods if that's your cup of tea.   Cardinal sin by the game makers: There's no save and quit option. You can save all you want, but when you hit the 'exit game' button it gives you the jackass 'are you sure? unsaved stuff might be lost' warning. Seriously Owlcat? Make save and quit an default function, it's 2020. If you want people to have the option not to save then make an extra button.

Не ожидал вообще от первого Фар Край такого хардкора. Думал, что это будет типичный стрелковый аттракцион. На деле враги то не видят тебя сквозь низкополигональные кусты, то пулемётом косят через палатку...Они вроде бы и косые, но каждая пуля приносит очень много боли, поэтому бронежелет был моим бро, и снайперская винтовка, и кусты, и...камешек. Добрую половину игры провёл за методичным отстреливанием вражин из кустов, передвигаясь аки ниндзяго. Время от времени тебе не оставляют выбора(особенно в конце трэш), и начинается форт боярд: вот тут вот увернись от ракеты, тут не попади под шквал пуль, на дельтаплане полетай...но я бы не назвал это весельем. Прицеливание через оптику доставило геморроя, и я так и не понял баг это или фича: иногда при передвижении он убирается, а иногда нет. С русской версией я потрахался и решил на английской остатся(в английской речь в целом не сложная, сюжет понятен, но она почему-то тише, чем остальное окружение) + если у тебя раскладка не переключена на ENG и ты запускаешь игру, то нужно будет сбрасывать настройки управления, RUS не распознаётся никак. Антураж, конечно, выбран удачно: красивые тропические острова, которые разбавляются время от времени ржавыми посудинами, секретными лабораториями и древними руинами. И тут я понял: это Crysis! Точнее Crysis это FarCry с навороченной графикой и супер костюмом - песочница один в один (ну и вместо монстров - пришельцы). Графика смотрится хорошо, музыка есть, но она не чувствуется(всё что я запомнил, это криповый звук открывающийхся дверей :D). Есть пара сюжетных поворотов, но я бы не сказал, что в целом захватывающий дух сюжет. Разнообразие врагов и хороший арсенал это несомненно плюс для этой игры. Поэтому игру рекомендую для ознакомления.

This is one of the most enjoyable games I have ever played and I've played a lot. What I like about the game is that the action is immediate and continuous;  it constantly surprises you with it's depth and new features and because of the complex spell system it gives you a ridiculous number of strategic options during any given turn.  The basic combat system is similar to Civilization,  but really more like Heroes of Might and Magic,  although it does not have separate explore modes to combat modes.  Resources are critical in this game.  It is expensive to research and use spells and to hire heroes and combat units.  The number of towns you can build is normally limited so it's quality not quantity that's important.  Placing your town near critical rare resource items is a must.  Similarly it is quality not quantity in your choice of units to recruit or build.  Experience upgrades, equipment upgrades and other perks are the key to victory.  Again that creates a lot of strategic use of your resources and upgrades.  By contrast I find the more highly rated age of wonders 3 plodding and just plain boring. This game can be chaotic.  It keeps you on your edge.  Age of wonders 3 is about spamming units towns and sucking resources.  It's just flat, not sure why.  It's just unfortunate that this game was not promoted very well.  The sales were too low and the series is now dead.  Paradox has abandoned it.

Je ne connaissais pas du tout l'univers et je n'ai pas accroché au premier abord au style graphique, ce jeu trainait dans ma liste de souhait depuis quelque temps et faute de jeux comblant mon ennui j'ai décider de donner à ce jeu une chance...  Je ne m'attendais pas du tout à découvrir un jeu de carte hyper stratégique, avec de la musique de malade et un univers aussi intéressant retranscrit par les différentes cartes composant les decks (un héros = un deck).   Le jeu s'explique bien, soit en lisant le tuto pour apprendre les règles, soit en apprenant pas à pas les ficelles de ce jeu dans une partie/tuto avec un début scripté. Puis tu es lâché, tu lances une partie en choisissant un ennemi (4 dans le jeu de base qui ont un gameplay assez différent les uns des autres), un groupe de 3 à 5 héros (l'objectif et les règles de la partie seront adapté en fonction du nombre de héros) et un environnement qui aura son propre deck et jouera des cartes à chaque tour, parfois t'aidant, parfois non, dépendant de la situation, c'est au joueur de s'adapter et répondre du mieux possible à ces événements. Le jeu est très bien fignolé (tout ce que tu as envie de savoir avant de faire un coup est visible facilement) et les parties sont d'une grande profondeur.  Il manque peut être un mode multijoueur en ligne (mais il est en construction), par contre en hotseat avec des amis vu la nature du jeu c'est parfaitement jouable.  Si toi aussi tu aimes la stratégie et le hasard n'hésites pas !

2014년 12월 스팀에 입점한 이 작품은 현재까지도 꾸준한 업데이트를 통해 게임에 덧살을 붙여나가며 현재, 거의 완성단계에 도달한 로그라이크  게임이다.  본인이 로그라이크 장르를 많이 해보지 못한관계로 다른 게임들을 비교하며 설명하기는 어려우나, 이 게임을 즐겼던 많은 유저들은 '스펠렁키' 에 멀티플레이와 장비수집, 기술습득과 같은 RPG의 요소를 가미한 게임이라 평하고 있다. 이 게임이 어떤 느낌인 감이 올 수 있는 평인듯 싶다.    [h1] 좋았던 점	[/h1]  - 특색있는 4가지 직업과 랜덤으로 나오게 되는 아이템들, 효능들로 다회차의 재미를 꾸준히 유지 - 고전게임처럼 숨겨진 요소들이 많아, 하나 하나씩 찾아내는 재미가 쏠쏠 - 플레이어와 멀티를 통해 협동 가능(최대 4인)  - 함정을 피해다니며, 보스들을 격파해나가는 도전적인 난이도가 매력적 - 아담한 용량과 낮은 요구사양 - 스팀 포럼에 상주하며 피드백을 받고, 답변을 주는 개발자(덤으로 게임 내 힌트도)   [h1] 별로인 점	[/h1]  - 던전이 생성될때 물체나 몹, 보스의 배치는 늘 바뀌지만, 맵은 랜덤생성이 아님.   그나마 여러 맵들이 준비되어 있지만, 수 시간 내에 똑같은 맵을 몇번이고 만나게됨 - 진행구성은 중간에 지하무덤으로 가지 않는한 변함이 없음. (동굴 -> 숲 -> ??? -> ??? ) - 게임 내 설명이 거의 없기에, 이런 불친절함에 당황해 할 수도 있음 - 불편하고 뻣뻣한 조작감. 캐릭터 모션 - 16.12.24 현재 게임은 미완성이라 버전이라, 게임엔딩도 없고 최종보스도 없음.   위에서 언급하였듯이, 이 게임의 단점과 장점은 정보부재에서 나오기도 한다. 이 점 덕에, 플레어이는 마치 모든것이 미스테리들로 가득했던 고전게임들을 하듯이 게임 내에 개발자가 감쳐둔 비밀들을 하나 둘씩 알아내며  흥미를 붙여나갈 수 있기도 하지만, 게임 내 접하게 되는 랜덤 요소와 조합,  사용법에 대한 정보가 없어 초보자들은 이런 불친절함에 게임 초반을  넘기지 못하고 방황할 수 있는 문제가 되기도 한다. ex) 독 포션은 '적용'버튼을 눌러 무기에 바를 수 있지만, 게임 내엔 아무런 설명이 없다.     심지어 개발자도 이 사실을 몰랐으면 했는데 라는 반응의 댓글을 달기도.  결국 포럼이나 위키를 찾아봐야 하는데, 그렇게 되면 게임의 재미가 급감하기 때문에 공략을 선택할 것인가 게임의 재미를 중시할 것인가 대한 딜레마에 빠지기 쉽다.  그 외의 문제는 게임이 미완성이라, 수백번의 죽음을 거쳐 게임에 익숙해진뒤에 게임의 위험들을 헤쳐나간뒤 끝에 도달한 순간, 축하 메세지 이외에 아무것도 없었다는점. 개인적으로 허무함을 감출 수 없었다.   그래도 게임은 거의 완성단계에 도달한것으로 보이며 현재는 마지막 부분 추가작업과 직업간의 밸런스 조절, 함정 추가 정도가 이루어지고 있기에 정식 출시를 기대해봐도 되지 않을까 생각해본다.  같이 할 친구가 있다면 서로 어려운 난이도에 처절함을 맛보며 게임을 진행해나가는 재미가  상당할듯 싶은데 혹여나 같이 게임을 해볼 친구가 있다면 이 게임도 나쁜 선택은 아닐것이다.   개인 평가 3.8 / 5.0

Estaba buscando un juego en Pc que me hiciera recordar esos fantasticos plataformas de la era los 32 y 64 bits que un look mas actual y he quedado maravillado con A Hat in Time que toma varios elementos de Super Mario Sunshine pero con su propia personalidad.  El juego en general me ha encantado los niveles son super coloridos y muy diferenciados entre ellos, los personajes tienen su carisma, el gameplay es intuitivo aunque alguna pequeña queja con la camara.  Al principio no me gusto el rendimiento del juego pero hay que mover algunos ajustes para lograr los 60 fps estables que se agredecen en juegos como este.  PROS: * El estilo grafico simplista pero realmente bonito y cumplidor * La variedad de mundos y mecánicas dentro de ellos aseguran que cada uno sea una experiencia distinta y novedosa. * El diseño y arquitectura de nivel en cada acto y capítulo son simplemente geniales. * Cada nuevo sombrero y medalla te animan a querer sacar todo en el juego antes de terminarlo. * El gran humor y carisma de los personajes mantiene al título entretenido de inicio a fin. * La version de steam con MODS es genial, hay algunos bastante buenos aparte de la traduccion que oficialmente no tiene.  CONTRAS:  * La cámara es un poco dura de mover y en muy pocos casos puede traer problemas. * El juego puede sentirse corto mas que nada por el reducido numero de niveles pero completarlos al 100 te puede entrener un rato mas si asi lo quieres. * El rendimiento del juego no es todo lo bueno deberia siendo que es un juego que ulitza un motor viejo como el UE3, hay que moverle algunos ajustes para correrlo fluido.

En 2014 sorti Mercenary Kings, un jeu qui me faisait de l’œil mais qui m'a énormément déçu manette en mains à cause de son gameplay lent, assez pauvre et de sa trop grande répétitivité. Trois ans plus tard, les mêmes développeurs, Tribute Games, sortent Flinthook : un rogue-like mélangeant plate-forme et run and gun. Ayant lancé le jeu sans en attendre grand-chose je dois dire que j'ai été surpris positivement par le titre sur de nombreux aspects.  La première grosse différence que l'on ressent entre Mercernary Kings et Flinthook est le gameplay. Bien plus rapide, exigeant et technique par rapport à Mercenary Kings, Flinthook envoie très vite son aîné ad patres pour notre plus grand bien. Malheureusement, ce même gameplay se révèle être perfectible sur quelques points bien particulier, notamment dans sa précision. Flinthook (qui est à la fois le nom du jeu et du personnage principal) possède, en plus de son pistolet et de sa chrono-ceinture (permettant de ralentir le temps), un grappin ; Si il est intéressant de noter que le grappin possède plusieurs fonctions intéressante au sein du titre comme celle d'ouvrir les portes, retirer le bouclier des ennemis ou bien évidemment de s’accrocher aux... crochets, il est à noter que ce même grappin pourra s'avérer être un calvaire à utiliser dans les tableaux mettant en scène de nombreux crochets et ennemis avec un bouclier : le grappin s'accrochant parfois sur un crochet à côté de l'ennemi et non pas sur le bouclier de celui-ci, nous faisant perdre quelques points de vie dans l'action.  Autre problème, la lisibilité. Outre le fait que je n'ai rien à dire sur la partie graphique en général, qui est loin d'être désagréable à l’œil au passage (la DA est globalement très bonne), ça m'est arrivé très souvent de me prendre un élément du décor que je n'avais pas vu dans le feu de l'action, les développeurs auraient clairement pu gommer ou corriger en partie ce défaut.  Concernant la difficulté en règle général, les développeurs ont eu l'intelligence de ne pas tomber dans le piège du débilement punitif. Si les premiers run du jeu pourront s'avérer difficile, le jeu ne fait pas l'erreur de nous foutre des multitudes de salles avec des ennemis qui nous martyrisent ou avec une multitude d'éléments du décor qui nous font perdre trois quarts de notre vie en la traversant. De surcroît, à l'instar d'un Rogue Legacy, il est possible d'acheter de manière permanente, entre chaque run, des améliorations pour notre personnage comme de nouveaux accessoires, des points de vie supplémentaires ou encore de nouveaux emplacements pour nos atouts.  Concernant la durée de vie, le jeu est bien plus long qu'on ne pourrait le croire. Bien que ne possédant que cinq niveaux et un mode de difficulté supplémentaire, dit féroce, à déverrouiller pour chacun d'eux, le jeu m'a pris environ 35 heures pour débloquer la totalité des succès du titre (hors ceux liés à la collecte d'objets), demandant entre autre de terminer chaque niveau avec un score minimal, sous un temps défini, de battre tous les boss en mode de difficulté maximal ou encore de débloquer la seconde fin du jeu... N'en attendez pas trop du scénario par contre. Entre autre, comptez une quinzaine d'heures de jeux si vous souhaitez simplement le terminer en ligne droite, ce qui reste tout de même très raisonnable.  En bref, bien que loin d'être imperfectible, Flinthook s'est révélé être un jeu très sympathique qui a su m'accrocher plusieurs dizaines d'heures. Je recommande.

Short version -   +Intriguing story & storytelling method +Breathetaking graphics & environments +Splendid soundtrack +Fluid gameplay, usually just about the right difficulty +A thoughful product, trying to truly deliver some content and idear relevant to everyday lives.  -Some players may find this to be a very long walking simulator -Gameplay could get repetitive at times -No replay value, gamplay-wise +\- You're basically all alone in the game, story usually unfolds in a very certain way through listening to voices\stories in the background (not always, but mostly). Depending on your style, you may or may not like it. Bottom line though - HOLY SHIT THIS WAS AWESOME GO PLAY IT  Longer review: Having played another game from the same developers (Enslaved), at the beginning of Hellblade I feared it all felt too familiar. You walk, walk, walk, have some story, fight, fight, fight, solve some easy puzzle, and then again. And again. And again. I do believe that both games 'fall into the trap' of this 'formational', repetitive gameplay. While I feel Enslaved was a great game in its own way and would play it again some day, I ended up giving it a negative review, mainly for those reasons, and I had a feeling it's going to be the same for Hellblade.  How wrong I WAS ! As I delved deeper into the game it completely sucked me in. This time, Ninja made the experience so much more powerful and intriguing, that it got the better of the repetitive gameplay (which in itself wasn't bad at all).  Watching the Hellblade Feature video from inside the game gave some more insights and had impressed me very positively towards Ninja Theory.  Story & idea: Without too much spoilers, this game takes place in a Viking-era environment, and revolves around a yound woman suffering of mental disorder. The devs had actually done research and tried to deliver as much as possible the way psychotic people actually see, feel, sense the world around them, based on real-life experiences, and the result is extremely interesting.  Very early in the game you'll learn that most of the story would be delivered through the voices in your chatacter's head. This could be a downfall for some players and personally I found it a bit hard to get used to myself, as I usually expect some more active characters and NPCs in a plot. But, you either got to love it or hate it. This game leaves you all alone with your character's perception of life, and that serves well the idea it tried to deliver.  Technical stuff: No complaints here at all. Even bad reviews usually admit that the graphics are magnificent. Soundtrack was amazing as well and I'm quite disappointed it is not officially released for listening. Didn't encounter any bugs or technical difficulties running the game (although it's a bit of resources hog!). Artistically and 'gamingly' you could say this game is a work of art.  Gameplay: As I have already mentioned, this is probably the weaker point of the game, and yet it's actually not bad at all. The game is indeed very story driven and it shows, so, of course that only gamers which are into this kind of thing would find it enjoyable. The levels are usually very linear. You would basically walk around and solve various puzzles, which regard mainly finding shapes in the environment around you, and the way Senua sees things around her. In-between there are battles, of course. There are also some runes you can collect to hear some more side stories, which are not too difficuly to find and still you may easily miss them if you don't actually look for them. Puzzles could get tedious for some BUT, I think the devs had wisely added some tiny twists to them, and evolved it a bit every time, and that made the entire thing playable. Yes, they still feel repetitive, and somehow it still wasn't like doing EXACTLY the same thing over and over. Which is good as you may spend a good 6-10 hours playing the whole game once, depending on your gaming style. The combat system however, didn't evolve throughout the entire game. Not sure whether it's a good or a bad thing, because making it too complicated could easily distract you from the main game and story. Still, it does get tiring. Luckily, the animations and moves were so fluid and aesthetic, so, for me, it was quite fun all the way through.  Replay &  Test of time: As mentioned earlier, gameplay wise there's not any replay value. The game would play exactly the same the next time you'd play it. I would definitely want to give it another go, though, sometime in the future. If you're into storytelling and immersion you'd definitely want to experience this game more than once. It was seriously quite an amazing experience which I recommend to most gamers out there.  Game's quite new, but I have a feeling it's one of those titles which are going to look & feel good, and even stay unique, quite some time after.   Summary: Most importantly, this game shows that small companies can also produce some (very) high quality product, which is also about good storytelling and experience, and about delivering a meaningful message, and not just relentless & empty action. Hellblade: Senua'a Sacrifice courageously touches a highly sensitive matter which is rarely presented in media and\or in video games specifically. Hope to see more quality products from Ninja Theory in the future!

[h1]Despite some minor UI/graphical hiccups, this game is well worth the small price: realistic, high-stakes, rewarding and educational. Best emergency sim I've played, perhaps ever.[/h1]  Anyone just playing the tutorial would be forgiven for thinking this game is a clunky mess: it throws you in, gives you some random stuff to do without much explanation, and the instructions aren't terribly clear at times (a certain point where you have to rewind to a previous stage has caused a lot of people trouble in the Discussions).   But if you stick with it, and put your mouse sensitivity up to max to cope with the admittedly janky CPR/ventilation mechanic, the game opens up into a [b][u]massively rewarding, and somewhat chilling, recreation[/u][/b] of what could very much happen in a car accident.  The realism is pretty incredible, and the [b][u]puzzle-like cases[/u][/b] means that you feel a real sense of accomplishment when you manage to save the victims and piece together the cause of the accident.  A bonus I didn't expect from the game is that it's FULL of [b][u]very useful tips[/u][/b] for what you should do if you come across an accident in real life. I'm only three cases in (of a current nine, with more planned) and I've learned a ton of stuff that every driver should know.  Finally, a small point, but for a Polish developer the [b][u]English is top-notch[/u][/b], nearing perfect. It's not important but I've played some European games where the translation has ruined the immersion somewhat.  [b][u]Can't go wrong with this - price is very reasonable, and for Early Access it's really quite advanced.[/u][/b]

Dafür bietet XCOM2 viele gelungene Neuerungen, unter anderem den Verborgenheitsmodus in Kombination mit dem Zeitdruck in vielen Missionen, wodurch das Spiel sehr actionreich und herausfordernd wird. Wahrscheinlich wird noch ein größerer Add-On dazu kommen, der das Spiel noch besser macht.  Was das Spiel außerdem sehr gut macht, sind die Mods. Endlich gibt es einen Karteneditor, sodass man im Steamworkshop sich noch mehr Kartentypen downloaden kann! Natürlich gibt es einige negative Aspekte des Spiels, die ich in diesem Review nicht erwähnt habe wie z.B. die anspruchsvolle Grafik, die nicht allzu große Abwechslung bei den Missionstypen, etc...  Aber dass ich XCOM2 nach über 200h Spielspaß immer noch sehr liebe, sagt doch schon viel aus. :D

Pour les -: - Après Rome II on retrouve le système de gestion par région ce qui fait qu'on doit tout avoir pour pas crever de faim, ou succomber à la peste, ou avoir un soulèvement...Le système ville par ville à la shogun ou rome 1, ou medieval 1-2 fonctionnaient bien...Ici on peut construire 6 batiments max dans la capitale de région et on est obligé de faire presque exclusivement le même truc pour toutes les régions pour ne pas avoir à stationner une armée dedans...  - Tout taxe de la bouffe ou de l'hygiène ressources de base de l'empire, mais des fois c'est tellement abusé qu'on fait que ça de la bouffe et de l'hygiène et on verra après si y'a moyen de faire du fric autrement. Phasmophobia ist ein außergewöhnliches Horror-Abenteuer.   Als mein Bruder mir von diesem Spiel erzählt hat und ein Gameplay gezeigt hat, fand ich das Spiel ziemlich interessant.  Im Anschluss habe ich einen Blick auf Steam geworfen um den Preis die Bewertungen in Erfahrung zu bringen. Äußerst Positiv? o.O Das Spiel sah zwar interessant aus, aber technisch bei weitem nicht so geil dass man es als Äußerst Positiv erwartet hatte. Nicht mehr lang gefackelt, haben wir und das Spiel gekauft und waren Äußerst Positiv überrascht^^^ Ich kann euch raten es selbst zu Spielen wenn ihr das Game interessant findet, denn erst dann merkt man weshalb das Spiel solch gute Rezensionen bekommt.   Sei ein Geisterjäger wie die beiden in Insidious! Rüstetet euch mit einer Cam, Geisterbox und vielen weiteren Gadgets aus, die euch dabei helfen herauszufinden um welche Art von Geist es sich handelt. Jede Geisterart hat seine eigenen Merkmale. Wenn ihr etwas in Erfahrung gebracht habt, tragt dies in euer Tagebuch ein. Für jede richtige Antwort gibt es nach Abschluss des Levels Geld, womit ihr euch neue Ausrüstung kaufen könnt. Erkundet bis zu 4 verschiedene Gegenden - mehr kommen bestimmt mit Updates hinzu.   Ich Spiele es ohne VR-Brille und habe meinen Spaß...Das Spiel wirkt so real...weil die 4. Wand gebrochen wird. MAN KANN MIT DEN GEISTERN REDEN!!! Das ist wohl das beste an dem Spiel. Dadurch wirkt es so echt, als wäre auf einer realen Geistersuche. Die Atmosphäre in dem Spiel ist einfach großartig.   So gut das Spiel auch sein mag, natürlich ist nicht alles perfekt. Die Grafik ist nicht die geilste, aber ausreichend. Man muss bedenken dass es in VR Spielbar ist. Die Renngeschwindigkeit unterscheidet sich nur um einen halben Schritt zur normalen Laufgeschwindigkeit. Die Animationen sind hässlich aber dafür sau lustig^^  Ich freu mich auf weitere Updates und bin sehr gespannt, was noch alles ins Spiel kommen wird. <3  Möchtest du mehr Meinungen von mir lesen? Dann folge meinem Kurator! https://store.steampowered.com/curator/28779772-JonnyDante-VIP-Lounge/  Du kannst auch bei meiner Partnergruppe vorbeischauen. Dort gibt zu ein paar Hundert Reviews, auch von anderen. https://steamcommunity.com/groups/hoi4deu

I have played every version of Civ since the very first one.  Some have been great, some mediocre, with the mediocre ones generally having some sort of game mechanic that just didn't work.  I really wanted to like Civ 6, but sadly I am finding it to be one of the mediocre versions.  There were so many new mechanics introduced into the game that I thought it would provide fresh challenges, but after numerous attempts to play through (and I have never managed to play through to a victory yet) I am finding the new mechanics to be akin to wading through mud.  The inspiration system for tech and social research seemed interesting, but I have found that it forces me into a fixed set of actions, decisions and sequences in order to trigger the inspirations (building two galleys when I really do not need them, building spearmen and carefully keeping a wounded barbarian around for it to kill, etc). When one falls behind in triggering inspirations, then one ends up repeatedly researching half of an advance and then switching to anther while waiting to trigger the inspiration.  The districts and wonders taking up tiles seemed interesting, but in reality this makes constructing them laborious and often leaving one feeling frustrated when a new district/wonder becomes available and only then finding that its tile restrictions conflict with other choices made before one even knew about the restrictions.  It also makes the selection of city sites difficult because there is no easy way to see which districts/wonders can be constructed from a particular site.  A related problem is that a district/wonder has to clear any terrain features to be built, but the only way to get the resource benefit of clearing the feature is to use a builder first before starting the construction.  A tool item to allow one to inspect tile restrictions for districts/wonders from the builder or city menu *before* one starts looking to build the item would help greatly.  Limited use builders also seem pointless.  They are literally nothing but a proxy the city's build queue - meaning one might as well simply have tile improvements be something that appears directly in the build queue instead of putting a limited builder in the queue and then building 3 to 5 improvements which then wanders over to build the improvement.  One can directly compute the build-queue cost of a tile improvement by taking the cost of a builder and dividing it by 3 (or 4 or 5 depending on wonders, civics, etc).  Having a limited-use builder unit that moves around on the map is really pointless.  Resource tiles seem particularly scarce. I find that when iron or niter turn up they are no where near any of my cities on a regular basis.  Roads are less useful because they are built by trade routes instead of builders (eventually one can use a Military Engineer, but I've not played long enough to get to that stage).I thought it would be an interesting mechanic (as it reflects reality) but in practice one simply does not end up with roads where one wants them.  Also, in the early game at least, they provide very little movement benefit.  Movement in general feels slow and build queues feel slow as well, which for me gives the game a slogging through mud feeling.

I'm giving this a negative review because sadly I feel the negatives outweigh the positives listed below.  The game has changed, and in a lot of ways, I feel like it has gone in the wrong direction. But as of recently, they have been changing the game to add back some features that players have asked for, and it has honestly put hope in my eyes.  Here are the good things (not going to list all the small things, just the impactful ones).   The tech tree gives players a sense of progress and specialization. Players can unlock the items they want, and aren't just sent down a pre determined path of leveling that they have no control over.  The tier system is good, it separates different builds and allows you to better understand how you're performing in relation to other players with similar level builds. This is pushed further by the competitive aspect which actually counts for each tier (from what I can tell). For instance, you can absolutely destroy everyone in tier 4, but in tier 3 you might be trash. This allows for an exciting competitive play for even new players, as they can rank up against similar builds and get the same experience as higher tier players.  I still like the community builds where people can upload their creations and get money when other people choose to use it, but it also feels way too chaotic. There's so many crafts that it seems pointless to upload your own because it will just be lost in the void of seemingly infinite crafts. I don't know how they could change this, but it almost seems like it needs to be thinned down and with a different upload requirement, but I honestly have no clue, I just know it could be improved.  The weapon variation is very nice. You have a lot of different weapons to choose from which can satisfy your need for variation, as they do all act quite differently.    Now for the bad, and what I think RoboCraft needs.  The first thing I think is needed has to do with the game play. It's fun to think of all the ways to work on progression and such, but if the actual game play is lacking, there's no point. ONE WEAPON PER CRAFT. This was a thing previously in RoboCraft, and I guess some people thought it was limiting people's creativity. This may be true, but I think the ability to have multiple types of weapons is actually limiting people's competitiveness and actual tactics. The main problem with this is to do with healing. You used to not have self-auto-healing in the game and instead the matchmaking would put healers on each team (the matchmaking tried to put the same amount of each different types of weapon crafts on each team, like 2 smgs, 2 plasmas, 1 sniper and a healer or such). The existence of these healers means that they were the ONLY way to heal your damaged parts. This meant that teams would actually stick together, and work together. It wasn't because the players were more competitive or better at the game. It was because that was the only way to get healed, so you just had to stick together, or at least be aware of where each teammate was. The game play as it currently stands (for me at least) consist of everyone corner peaking, doing damage, taking damage, then just waiting for heals. The game modes themselves even take away from this. Team deathmatch has respawns, as well as the domination game mode. So there's no real punishment for dying or taking damage, other than a little wait time before you're right back into it. Even if you took out self healing, everyone can just throw a healer on their craft alongside all their weapons, and just switch when someone takes damage. People would stick together (to some extent), but it would just be pointless to actually make a craft that only heals. In the current game mode, Pure healers exist (crafts with only healing guns), but it's kind of pointless for the average game. Noone cares enough about the damage they take, because eh, just hide for a few seconds. The amount of flyers is also insane because they just fly away and heal, it's too easy.   I honestly think that they need to at least bring out the game mode where you only have one life, with those 3 lane maps we all remember and the bases that could be captured if players were left broken and hiding. Along with this, maybe over time to see if it works or not, as to not just rush and assume it doesn't work, either get rid of or rework the auto heal or limit the weapons allowed on each craft.  PLEASE GET RID OF INFINITE ITEMS. This one is just dumb, it takes away 99% of the reason to play. If you can have infinite of the items, what am I grinding for? What am I aiming for? Just xp? I want to have to buy each part I put on my craft, I don't want these free things that make the game feel like a lottery, and I hate just having everything. I want a goal in the game.  I don't hate the devs, and I don't hate the game, I hate what happened to it. It felt like for a long while they just got rid of every feature in their game, and it honestly just feels empty and less complete than it did 4 years ago, which shouldn't be the case. I LOVE that the devs are actually listening to players and bringing back features, but they need to do more, and I'm willing to stick around if they do.   MORE THINGS  This is a questionable one, but I'll tell you why and everyone else can decide. The game use to have different level cubes, and you would have to buy every single one. They had set colours, which meant you could tell what level they were, and towards the end game, they got EXPENSIVE. I remember playing with my friend every night after school, and after each match, we'd be able to change like one cube to the next level, and we slowly got to see our craft be upgraded, and get stronger. You could just throw high level guns on and progress up, but you wouldn't be able to tank many shots. I honestly loved this grind and actual sense of progress as my craft would upgrade block by block and I could visually see this change. Now the game just scales up the blocks from what I can tell, and you have an infinite amount. That entire part of the game, gone.   Gamemodes. 100% they need to bring back the boss battles. It was honestly so cool being a high enough level that your craft was considered a boss and you would go out and battle like 6 lower tier players all fighting against you. That was insanely fun and when I was a lower tier player, it gave me another goal. A goal to get powerful enough that I could be that guy. I could be the boss. I said earlier they need the one life game modes too. I think that's a must have for just the game at its standard, not even as an extra, but a core element.   If I think of something else, or if they change the game, I will be sure to update this, as above all else, I want this game to get better, as I've seen the potential already. The fact that I think the game use to be one of my favourite all time games, and now it's almost the worst, hurts so much. I want the game to succeed.  Please comment if I'm wrong about anything, and I will be sure to change it, or argue like a little baby in the comments. Thankyou for reading, and thank you RoboCraft for actually making changes.

As much as I love the historic setting games, this was the marriage of IP's many had been waiting for, and it does not dissapoint. A dose of freshness to what was fast becoming a stale brand. Having played TW since the very first shogun, it hit a high watermark (for me) in medieval II, then began going downhill. Attila was a brief glimpse of hope, and then finally the TW brand hit another high by going fantasy.  My only caveat is that the battles are still just that tiny bit too fast and arcadey. But gladly nowhere near the dopy turbo speed of Shogun II, where all the ashigaru have been at the methamphetamines. Battle speed is not an easy balance. Realistically, most one on ones end at a single stroke - but TW has maybe gone a bit too far at times (Shogun II) and represents this accurately, whilst failing to address the way warriors might tentatively approach one another as combat commences. There is no fear of death in TW games before a unit breaks. I want my low tier units to be half in need of a change of trousers as they approach for the final clash.  This game has depth that works, where predecessors had depth that didn't (Empire/Napoleon). It streamlines where things might get boring, and expands on the interesting aspects - and this is a fancy feather in the cap for the devs, because it could have all gone so easily wrong here.  Diplomancy is still a bit meh, especially certain aspects of confederacy. It's all a bit 'gamey'. I would like to see some ideas from Paradox games implemented here.  The look is fantastic, tongue in cheek semi-grimdark that warhammer fantasy should be, and hats off to the artists and animators for that. Nail on the head stuff. Sound is also great, except for one offputting thing - the dwarf lords often sound like they are saying 'wankrag'.  Battlefields have amazing backgrounds, but the field itself is often somewhat bland and repetitive in terms of tactical options.  Unit variety is again fantastic, but I do not like how experienced units who have seen many battles can be matched and even outdone by higher tier building units. I feel that there needs to be two levels of experience - rather than the single line of chevrons that we have - combat experience and training level on seperate lines maybe.  All in all, the devs should be proud of a job well done. After the debacle of Rome II I was afraid it was going to be another failure. But they turned the tables and made a new classic TW.

Have you played Ufo Defense? Then you've played Terror From the Deep. It's still a good game, but only because the first one was a good game already. Being completely fair the game is basically Ufo Defense with an underwater skin. Names are different, set pieces have the subaquatic feel but the core gameplay is still the same. Down to the fact it expects you to really know how to play before even booting it up. But is there anything new to it besides the sea theme? A bit, but not much.  There are two new types of missions, both with two levels. The research tree is a bit more complex, with a bunch of pre-requisites for some of the threes and what I could say are some new types of equipment. The last level is also bigger than Ufo Defense's and less easy to cheese (sadly no 1-turn wins for this one, it seems), but the core idea is still the same. The ending itself is a lot more confusing as well, where the first game left you with a more conclusive and well-explained story this one is more focused teasing the third one instead of giving a better-explained ending sequence.  In the end, if you enjoyed Ufo Defense you'll most likely enjoy Terror From the Deep, as long as you don't expect anything new. For me? I'd say if I wanted to play Ufo Defense I'd just play it. SO while the game is not bad, I can't say it's recommended.

For example, in Rise of the Samurai and the main game, your fame will work against you, but there are benefits to becoming famous in Fall of the Samurai. The in-game encyclopedia is both helpful and information containing fun history bits about when certain things came in to being or how gameplay and history may differ.  It's excrutiatingly detailed and perhaps a bit hardcore, but if you're willing to sit down and figure out how the game works, you'll be pleasantly rewarded.  Full disclosure: The difficulties don't lie. Easy is rather easy and plays to your favor but the Hard Modes will buff the bots and they'll use better decision making AI. You've been warned.

Hundreds of playing cards float in a rotating mass above the table. As you approach, a mysterious hooded figure greets you, and invites you to play a game. This is no ordinary game, however. You will be playing with Fate, the most fickle of mistresses.   Hand of Fate presents itself as a seemingly simple rogue-like card game. Face down cards act as the playing board, and each turn you move your figure on the board to a new card. As you reach new cards, they are revealed and you must face whatever challenge Fate decides to hand you. It could be a simple peasant begging for food, a shop where you can restore your health and food supply in exchange for gold, or any number of hostile encounters. Often, you are presented with some choice, and based on your choices (and your fortune) there will be consequences.   Combat is played out in real time, which is a nice addition. However, the combat itself leaves a lot to be desired, so if the rest of the game doesn't sound interesting to you, the combat will not make it any better. Most of the time you're either spamming dodge or spamming counter if you have a shield (although later on some of the attacks become unblockable). While not the most fluid combat system ever, it is serviceable enough and helps to keep the game more than just praying to RNGesus (praise be to He).  However, what this game lacks in technical polish, it more than makes up for in style and originality. The mysterious host is always giving commentary, injecting a bit of sass into your escapades. This game is at its most exciting when you are discovering something new; even though you get to build your encounter and equipment decks before the game begins, you won't know what a new card does until you find it inside the game.  I would recommend this game to anyone who loves good story-telling, atmosphere, and leaving your destiny to the whims of fate. Stay away if you dislike reading, clunky combat, or can't stand RNG.  They say fortune favors the bold, so go ahead and try your luck.

このゲームのレビューに不評が投じられる理由は以下の通りです。  ・公式サーバーでプレイしている ・シングルプレイを初期設定のままでプレイしている ・コンソール版発売と同時に定価が急上昇した事に不満を訴えている ・低スペックのPCでグラフィック設定を変更せずプレイしている ・開発元＝販売元のゲームのよくある頻繁なアップデートに対応出来ない ・海外ゲーによくあるガバガバな物理演算、地形スタックなどに慣れていない ・UIに不満がある  率直に申し上げてこれらを理解・解決できる方であればおススメ出来るゲームと言えます。 あとは好みの問題です。  シングルだろうがマルチだろうが、初期設定は変更すべきでしょう。 元々大人数でのプレイを前提に作られていますので、 ゲームを進めれば進めるほど非常に多くのリソースを要求されます。 それは素材だけではなく時間も同じです。  少なくとも「テイム時間」「素材の取得量」「経験値倍率」「夜の長さ」 「ホストテザー距離（マルチでのホストから離れられる距離）」 この辺りは変更してプレイすべきです。 シングルならなおさら、フレンドとプレイするのであっても誰も責める事はありません。 これはチートではなくゲームバランスの調整です。 ○ンスター○ンターだってプレイヤーの人数で敵のHPが変わるんですからそれと同じです。  ■2018/03/24追記 たくさんのレビュー好評を頂きましたので、 設定例としていつも遊んでいる環境設定を記載しておきます。 2・3人でプレイする場合の設定です。 【一般】 経験値倍率：2.0（レベルが80近くなると急に渋くなるので4.0にしたりも） テイム速度：4.0~8.0 建造物修理のクールタイム：5.0 採取量：2.0 プレイヤー/恐竜の体力回復速度：2.0 非専用ホストテザー距離：100.0　※必須！ （非専用ホストでのマルチ時にホストから離れられる距離ですが、 洞窟などはホストが入ると他プレイヤーも強制移動するので注意） 複数のプラットフォームフロアを許可：ON  【詳細】 疾患の非永続化：ON 赤ちゃんの刷り込み抱擁を誰でも許可：ON 交尾間隔：0.5 卵の孵化速度：2.0 夜間の経過速度：1.5 （慣れてきたら1.0に戻して良いかも、 初期マップとThe Center以外のマップをプレイする場合は初期から1.0推奨） 作物の成長速度：2.0 作物の腐敗速度：0.5 ダメージ値のテキスト表示：ON（個人的には必須だと思っています） プラットフォームの建築数制限の増加：5.0（イカダを拠点にして旅したい方へ）  ----------  このくらいの設定で甘口寄りの中辛って感じです。 難易度が高い洞窟はメチャクチャ辛いですし、かといって絶望的な程ではありません。 適切な装備や食料を持ち込んで挑めば命からがらクリアできる、くらいの難易度です。 ただし、Aberrationマップだけは難易度桁違いなのでお覚悟を…。

Если у каждой последующей цивы графика эволюционировала, то в 6 графика скатилась до уровня планшета. Выглядит не естественно и мыльно. Кому-то такая графика понравится но не мне. Тактический режим очень хорошо выглядит, вопросов нет. Любимый скайримчик да еще и переиздание с новыми текстурками!  Приятная, ламповая атмосфера, сказочный мир - наделенный своей завораживающей магией.  Сравнивать буду конечно же с Подливионом.  И так, что имеем: Боевая система потерпела изменения, она не стала лучше или хуже, она изменилась полностью. Теперь от безумных взмахов мечом налево и направо не осталось и следа. Анимация и физика узнали друг друга и теперь бои сделаны с уклоном на эффектность, а попасть по противникам стало сложнее, особенно в игре от 3 лица, так как камера от персонажа переехала немного вправо.  Алхимия и зачарование были изменены. Зачарование стало доступнее, его можно улучшать. Алхимия теперь не всегда с вами, а только на специальном столике. Магические школы так же были изменены, некоторые заклинания были убраны и заменены на зачарование. Новая система перков стала более широкой и дает огромное количество бонусов игроку. Графика мне очень нравится, 8 шакалов из 10. Диалоги и интерфейс ооочень удобные и прекрасно подходят как для клавиатуры так и для геймпада. Ну и пара слов о музыке - она прекрасна!  Это лишь малая доля нововведений, все перечислять можно сидеть до вечера пятницы. Багов тоже кстати завезли и не мало. То текстуры не прогрузятся, то напарники вход заградят, а то и вовсе пристанет какая-нибудь рыба в речке и будет до скончания веков играть боевая музыка. Квесты можно легко сломать по незнанке, но вроде консолью пользоваться не пришлось, все решаемо. Кстати, консоль в русской версии не работает.  Долго думал и все таки купил этот Special Edition. Игра уже была пройдена давным давно а 2012 году, но то было обычное издание и без всех официальных DLC. Играл очень долго и тщательно, собрал всю возможную экипировку, зачарования, зелья, прокачал все навыки до сотни, но все ачивки добить не хватило сил просто. Как говорится - я мухожук. Однозначно рекомендовано к покупке. Каждая копеечка вложенная в игру принесет вам радость и удовольствие!

Il est certes beau, surtout grâce au pixel art, mais l'esthétique ne colle absolument pas avec l'ambiance qu'essaye d'instaurer le jeu : C'est trop coloré, c'est trop clair. Où est l'ambiance sombre et dérangeante d'un diablo 1 ? Ou même d'un salt and sanctuary ?  Deuxième point sur lequel j'insisterai : Le gameplay est très rigide, et ne laisse place qu'à peu d'erreurs (plateformes je vous aime). Ce gameplay rigide est d'ailleurs empiré par un level design parfois très vicieux, on sent l'intention du développeur de nous faire mal.  Le cara design est très bof (j'ai parfois l'impression de jouer à Asterix), et c'est dommage... Surtout pour un jeu qui se veut dans un esprit gothique / sanglant.  Le jeu est assez lent dans son entièreté, et notamment contre certains ennemis.   Points positifs :  Certaines zones sont très agréables à explorer (d'autres sont des zones vues et revues, comme la montagne ou les égouts)  Le jeu est très beau (même si je n'aime pas le design général, il faut avouer qu'il est très bien soigné). Les musiques sont très agréables, même si elles ne resteront pas dans les mémoires.  La prise en main est rapide, malgré un manque de dynamisme.  Les combats de boss sont en général excellents (hormis le bébé à épines).  Je ne recommande pas ce jeu, car dans la même gamme de prix, on peut trouver bien mieux, comme Hollow Knight pour ne citer que lui. Je ne peux cependant pas dire que le jeu soit à jeter, il y a quelques heures à passer sur ce dernier.

Há muito tempo esperava esse jogo aqui na steam, e, não é que ele apareceu?!  Obscure é um game de Survivor Horror, lançado pela Hydravision em 2004. O jogo conta  a história de cinco jovens estudantes (Shannon, Ashley, Stanley, Josh e Kenny)  que em um belo dia acabam ficando presos no colégio Leafmore. A partir daí irão enfrentar inimigos obscuros e se depararão com uma  cadeia de informação pra lá de sinistra. De uma maneira resumida o game se apresenta com gráficos bons (para época que foi lançado) e as músicas, vozes e  efeitos sonoros são excelentes. Agora,  o carisma dos personagens é sem dúvida o ponto alto do game, pois nos faz envolver ainda mais com a trama! Quanto a jogabilidade é interessante observar que ela acerta quando propõe a mudança em qualquer momento entre os 5 personagens e também por permitir multiplayer local (jogar co-op com um amigo é bacana), mas erra feio na execução dos comandos, pois, definitivamente não é tarefa fácil jogar no PC (vai precisar ser persistente!). Outro ponto negativo é o sistema de câmera que é simplesmente ruim e ultrapassado (mesmo para 2004), deixando o jogo estressante em diversos momentos. Bom, sem mais delongas é o seguinte: se você é fã de games nos moldes Resident Evil, Alan Wake e outros mais, comprem, vale a pena!!

Despite some issues of framerate and glitches, this is a fantastic expansion to the previous Firaxis XCOM. Most of what has been done to the game is possitive, and even some of the more divisive of changes, such as the inclusion of so many mission timers, are at worst minor complaints. True, it would be nice to have a few more un-timed missions for the sake of sniper focusing and setting up elaborate ambushes, but for many missions the added drive to move helps the feel of this game as a leaner, meaner child of Enemy Unknown/Within.   Mechanically, it plays much like it's predecessor, and I can see anyone who played and enjoyed the first game being easily about to do so again, even if some of the more esoteric additions don't quite click. The tactical game is fantastic, with simple controls and a clean UI. At the stretegy level, things are a little less clear, likely due to this being the more experimental side of things. The way missions are presented can be distracting, and while functionaly the satelite system from the first game the territory system is less well presented and explained in-game. It all works, but be ready to make some mistakes and poor choices in your first game.   The real problem is in stability. I've not had a single crash as of hour 5, but certain missions have suffered from stuttering and bugs. It's easy to assign this to 'new game jank' but after being held back several months, you have to wonder how broken the game was when it was first meant to be released. Given Firaxis' history with XCOM, I can only assume it will be dealt with, or mitigated soon. Still, if you're not desperate to play right now, it may be worth waiting for a patch or two before getting started.   FINAL SCORE: YES OUT OF 10

I have spent many hours playing KTaNE, and even more working on custom content for the game, now, as a maintainer of [url=https://ktane.timwi.de]ktane.timwi.de[/url] and a developer of the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1711408527]Twitch Plays mod[/url] (possibly the most complex mod available), and with 10 of my own mods, I feel somewhat obligated to give a review.  [h1]Short Answer[/h1] 10/10 would recommend, even if you don't have the game yourself, find someone you can play it with.  [h1]Long Answer[/h1] KTaNE is unique in that it's a game that doesn't require you to own the game to be able to play it, it's a multiplayer game which requires only one person who's playing to own the game. The other players (the experts) are able to use the manual, which contains instructions on the module on the bomb, to allow the player with the game (the defuser) to defuse the bomb.  If you ever get bored of playing with the modules in the game, there are always mods on the steam workshop, we're now approaching 300 modules rapidly, and with new modules coming out almost every day, there's always something new to learn. Each modded module presents it's own challenge for the defusers and the experts to work out using the manual, which can all be located on [url=https://ktane.timwi.de]ktane.timwi.de[/url].  If you're still bored, there's always the Twitch Plays mod. This mod allows players to disarm modules and defuse bombs through the chat on [url=https://www.twitch.tv]twitch[/url]. There's always at least one stream going with the TP mod, so I would recommend checking this out.  Finally, if you're unable to find a defuser, or you're unable to find any experts to play with you, you can always use the [url=https://discord.gg/ktane]KTaNE discord server[/url]. There are many friendly faces there, and there's almost always someone ready to jump into a game with you.

Nie war Zombies töten einfacher als mit der Left 4 Dead Reihe. Ob man sich nun mit einer E-Gitarre oder einem Katana durch die Horden von Untoten kämpft ist egal, sie fallen wie geschnitten Brot. Das Spiel ist trotz der düsteren Atmosphäre und Situation in der sich die 4 Protagonisten befinden stehts ein Stimmungsheber. Man selbst wird Unterhalten durch coole Sprüche und schwarzen Humor von seinen Mitstreitern. Auch wenn das Spiel an einigen Stellen eintönig scheint, wird einem doch einiges geboten. Entweder man kämpft sich Online mit anderen durch Kampagnen und überwindet so den unangenehmen Zeitgenossen oder man wechselt die Seiten im Versus-Modus. Das Spiel ist ein klassisches Gelegenheitsspiel nicht mehr und nicht weniger. Wenn man sich durch Zombies kämpfen will ist man hier richtig, sucht man stattdessen nach tiefgründiger Handlung oder ist Fan von Hintergrundinfromation so wird man hier leider enttäuscht. Aber sowas brauch L4D2 auch nicht um ansprechend zu sein. Zombieliebhaber werden es mögen, andere werden es einmal Spielen und vielleicht nie wieder anrühren.

Never thought I'd leave a review like this since I've always scoffed at similar ones. Those who state they wouldn't recommend the game in spite of playing it for so long and enjoying so many aspects of it, however I am now a part of that large group.  I WOULD recommend this game to people who don't care about finishing a game and just wanna enjoy it, but I wouldn't recommend the game to anyone who wants to complete it having sunk so long into it.  Basically long story short, I don't play games for their difficulty but instead for their story, so I played on the easiest mode and breezed through 95% of the game, until the end where even being level 16, having great gear and a strong team I was wiped over and over again by enemies I couldn't hit or who kept healing themselves.  The rest of the game is good, but the end game, (leading up to the very end I discussed above) was also very lacking, you end up skipping huge amounts of time in the Kingdom Manager, repeating the same events over and over again to pass the time till you can crack on with the final battle and it was during that point that I started growing bored for the first time.  Sorry devs, you made a good game, good story, characters and stuff but the end was just a massive let down for someone who wants to just enjoy the story.

Anno 1404 was a magical game. The setting was perfect for me. I love history, and that game scratched every itch I had. Everything made sense: Of course your pioneers needed fish. Of course they needed meat, coffee, wine and tools. The production chains made sense, I understood them. You need cows to produce meat. You need iron and wood to produce tools.   That is why Anno 2070 did not manage to suck me into it. That is one of the reasons Anno 2205 fails. Do you need nano ceramics and cobalt to produce construct-o-bots? I have no idea.   What I truly loved about the previous Anno games was this:   If you had joined a game after 20 hours, everything would seem like complete chaos. Fleets of ships going in all directions carrying tons of different goods to a dozen islands. But for the player, every little thing made sense. Because they had built everything from scratch. Every boat, every building, everything. That was the real beauty of it. The best learning curve I have ever witnessed in a game.   It was challenging. You had to keep trying getting the perfect balance in your production chains. You had the option to taxate the population and selling surplus goods. You had to fight for the best islands.  Now, they have stripped most of it out. Every warehouse is in prebuilt locations. The ships are just generated, making no sense. You cannot set taxes, you dont need to fix production chains as they tell you exactly what you need to do, and you cannot sell goods! So what do you do when you are low on cash? Its quite simple, actually: You just leave the game with a positive income, and let time take care of it.   That was the point when I realised how poor this game was: When I could leave the game on for several hours, and when I opened it again, the ONLY thing that had happened was a big bank account. In Anno 1404, that would have been a suicide. Pirates would attack. Other players would steal the best islands, they would invade you. The production chain was guaranteed to be a little off-balance, so after some hours your citizens would have left your town. Because they would run out of bread, meat and books. And I understood them. I would leave too.   Would I leave due to a lack of neuro implants? I dont know. Probably not.   This is not strategy, its barely administration. Bring back the excellent gameplay of 1404, and make a Anno 1800 or 720bc. Until then, I will keep beating the shit out of Leif Jorgensen.  PS: If you havent played Anno 1404, do it. Its the pinnacle of the series in my opinion, and it has aged quite well.

Windbound est un jeu au premiers abord sympathique de son point de vue graphique qui me fait penser à The Wind Waker que j'avais adoré et nous promet une belle aventure. Seulement au bout des premières heures on se rend compte que cette promesse est biaisé.  Une aventure très courte, très redondante et peu scénarisé. Au finale on ne comprend pas le but et l'histoire en elle-même.  Je vais résumer ici les point positif et négatif de mon point de vue après avoir terminée le jeu.   Point + : -La direction artistique est sympatique si on n'aime le style -L'évolution du système de craft du bateau et des objets est simple sans prise de tête : place limité dans l'inventaire donc des choix à faire. -L'aventure en elle-même est plaisante : évolution du personnage et du bestiaire équilibré -Menu inventaire et craft simple à prendre en main et lisible au premier regard  Point - : -Pas de keybinding possible : frustrant car on est imposé dans les actions des touches comme la course, le mode furtif, l'inventaire ou la carte. -Menu trop simple : pas de notice qui indique les touches pour chaque action. Exemple l'affichage de la MAP n'est pas indiqué et se fait via la touche M en clavier QWERTY!! -La MAP qui n'indique pas au minimum les îles à visiter donc on loupe surement des îles au cours de l'aventure -La navigation est une plaie à gérer surtout via la voile : souvent on finit par chavirer par-dessus bord -Bug de monstre qui finissent par s'envoler dans les airs quand on les tue : perte de loot -Bug de certaines recette de craft qui n'apparaissent pas automatiquement : flèche de fer, lance de fer.. -Jeu très redondant : même paterne d'îles répétitif -Bestiaire très pauvre : j’ai noté 5 race de « gros monstres », 3 race de monstres « classique », 3 race de monstres « inoffensif », 2 race de monstres « marin » sans interaction.  En résumé je note négativement ce jeu même si j'ai pris du plaisir à y jouer car on nous a promis (les Dev dans le Hub communautaire) une aventure d'environs 40h alors que j'ai terminé l'aventure en 13h environs en étant mort une fois (rebuild du bateau à faire, perte du stuff sur le bateau) et en ayant perdu une partie d'un autre bateau à cause d'un requin donc perte de stuff et reconstruction du bateau.  De plus je n'ai pas rush le jeu, j'ai pris mon temps pour explorer et j'ai quasi tout trouvé en craft et objets (certains objets je n'ai pas trouvé l'utilité : certaines plantes..)  Le jeu n'offre quasiment plus de surprise d'évolution/rebondissement après quelques heures, un scénario quasi inexistant et un bestiaire très pauvre. Selon moi il est trop chère 30€ pour ce qu'il a à offrir, il devrait être aux alentours de 20€ en comparant d'autre titre similaire. [h1]Introduction[/h1] 7 Days to Die is a survival-crafting game from indie developers and publishers, The Fun Pimps, currently in Early Access on Steam.   In 7 Days to Die you play one of few survivors in a post-apocalyptic wasteland. The decaying remnants of society are scattered about you, inhabited now by endless hordes of wandering zombies. You start the game on a bright, sunny morning in the desert in Arizona (or potentially another biome somewhere else, if you're playing a generated world) wearing your stylish underwear and carrying only a few odds and ends. It's up to you to find your way to shelter -- or make it -- and survive as long as you can in a hostile world.  [h1]Presentation[/h1] The graphics in 7 Days to Die are mostly excellent, with a range of great zombie models with good texturing and animations; believable lighting effects that differ convincingly between flame, electric lights, and ambient lighting; and a desolate world that really draws the player in.  Some of the graphics, though, are considerably less impressive up close, with much of the ground foliage being obviously made of a couple of flat planes with textures applied, stuck in the ground as if on a wooden cross; many of the building block textures being just a little too repetitive and plain; and a number of little graphical glitches, such as water containing weird sharp-edged shapes, occasionally disappearing textures, and some weird shadow effects visible on occasion.  The user interface is consistent and reasonably good looking, too, though it can be a bit confusing and fiddly. Even after hours of play I often find myself pressing LMB to place something in the world rather than RMB, and dragging items in the inventory sometimes requires a brief pause to pick something up, which took me a while to get used to. It's also much too easy to irretrievably destroy something important through accidentally dropping or throwing it.  Music is extremely limited, but not lacking, if that makes any sense. There's a minimalist title theme, which suits the game perfectly: lonely, mournful instruments that evoke a feeling of drama and loss. Other than that there are a few chords here and there, keyed off dramatic events occur as you play, but nothing else that I'd actually call a music track.  Sound effects are mostly really good. There are the usual tool crafting sounds -- axes, hammers, and whatnot -- as well as typical FPS sounds of exertion from running, jumping, and becoming tired. Zombie sounds are varied, and after a few encounters one learns to recognise zombie types by sound. Weapons sound convincing; I haven't yet managed to build any vehicles so I can't comment on them, but the occasional plane flying overhead sounds good. There are no voiceovers.  Graphics settings are numerous enough to customise performance vs quality to a range of PCs. I haven't encountered any persistent performance issues, though the game does stutter for a second or so when loading in new areas or spawning zombies and I found inventory performance was terrible when facing a river while also crafting a stack of short-timeframe materials.  [h1]Gameplay[/h1] The game gives you a brief tutorial, presented in the form of UI messages ostensibly received from a surviving human settlement, which should keep you busy for the first few hours of the first day, and see you kitted out with a club, a bow, an axe, and a few more goodies, all of your own making. Then it's up to you to find or build somewhere to live. Don't take too long, though, as come 22:00 it'll be getting very dark, and as we all know zombies like the dark ... . There's a reason the game is called 7 Days to Die, too, and it's a scary one. Survive until 10pm on Day 7 and you'll be rewarded with a rampaging, slavering horde of zombies who, under the influence of the weekly Blood Moon, are able to find you unerringly, wherever you may be hiding. Build up those defences; you're going to need them!   7 Days to Die is played from the familiar first-person view, and it takes much of its action from the FPS genre. I wouldn't call it a FPS, though; while there is indeed a lot of combat, to me the game is much more about building an intelligent defence from the scraps you find or can harvest than it is about shooting.  Typical play is cyclic, with your long days spent farming, mining, exploring, and scavenging, and your very dark nights -- when the zombies are most active and aggressive -- spent huddled next to a dim candle, recovering from the day's activities, crafting items, and, planning your next day's activities. Each week is cyclic, too, with the first six days and nights as described, but the seventh night spent praying your preparations were enough -- and defending your ramshackle base if they fail.  The pre-built world of Navezgane County, Arizona, is huge and it provides a lot to explore and do. I've been playing for about 20 hours so far and have built and reinforced a tiny base near my starting point, but have only explored a tiny portion of the map. Navigation is easy with the UI compass (there's no need to make your own, which would have been a cool addition to the game) and the map provides some pre-defined waypoints for things like traders or your bedroll (spawn point for when you die), as well as allowing you to specify your own.  You'll encounter a number of different types of zombies as you play, and as well as the Blood Moon horde every seven days you'll also come across roaming hordes randomly during the day. These can kill you just as dead, so be careful! The game is mostly fair, though; I've died twice so far -- strangely the game says three times -- and both times have been to my own stupidity.   The best part of the game in my opinion is the immersion. Nights are so dark that it can be really frightening huddled there in a corner with only a candle for light -- larger light sources are more likely to attract zombies -- while strange night noises surround you and you hope the shuffling zombie you can hear doesn't decide to investigate the door you didn't quite manage to repair. And while the scavenging, mining, crafting, etc, get very repetitive, they're very well done, and with so much to create! This is all helped by the renewed sense of purpose that each week brings.  As the game is still in EA, there are a number of bugs and other issues, the worst of which break this wonderful immersion. The worst is probably zombies who spawn inside sealed buildings, especially while you're in them. They also seem to know the weakest points in your defences, even if it all looks the same from outside. I'm not convinced about the attraction to light sources, either; placing torches in a completely light-sealed room seems to magically cause more zombie interest in your base. There are also the graphics issues I mentioned earlier.  [h1]Pros and Cons[/h1] Pros: + Fantastic, immersive, and huge game world + Great difficulty curve and game balance + (Mostly) good graphics + Steam Achievements and Trading Cards  Cons: - The interface can be a bit finicky - Some bugs, the worst of which destroy the immersion  [h1]Verdict[/h1] 7 Days to Die has been in Early Access on Steam for just over four years, but don't let that put you off; the still-very-active developers are simply using EA as a means to produce an excellent game with community involvement, exactly as it should be used.  If you enjoy survival-crafting games, can put up with some bugs as new game systems are introduced and refined, and don't mind killing a zombie or two (hundred), then you really shouldn't miss 7 Days to Die. It is an amazing game, EA or not.  Now, where was I? Oh, that's right; let's see what's inside that old motel ... . Eeek! Zombies! [h1]OVERVIEW[/h1] Alien Shooter TD is a tower defence game set in the Alien Shooter game world.  You're a commander in charge of Earth's defence forces as you try to wipe out the invading alien threat. You're given command of SWAT, marines, and various specialist military units, and with these paltry few, you have to save the planet.  [h1]Graphics[/h1] The game is played from a 3/4 top down view. Graphics look nice when zoomed out, but become a bit blurry and pixelated when you zoom right in. You'll spend most of the time zoomed out anyway.  The interface is fairly pretty and easy to use once you get the hang of a few intricacies. The tutorial shows you most of the functions and you can work out everything else fairly easily after that.  There are no graphics options to speak of: only full screen / windowed mode (requiring a restart of the game, for some reason), and an option to turn blood green. Performance-wise the game ran fine on my new gaming laptop, even with hordes of nasty alien scum on screen at once.  [h1]Sound[/h1] Sound is workable, but nothing too exciting. Gun sounds are good, and chittering alien death is satisfying. Music is forgettable, but unassuming.  [h1]Gameplay[/h1] The core gameplay in Alien Shooter TD is the same as every other tower defence game: place towers in set positions on the relatively small battle map in order to try to wipe out the aliens that travel along set routes. In the case of Alien Shooter TD, the towers are actually troops of different types, but the principle is the same.  In this game most levels have relatively few placement areas on the map, and there are only seven different troop types in all (with only one available to begin with), so your choices are sometimes quite limited. But you're shown the path the aliens will take in each wave, and units can be upgraded with training and skill trees, as well as improved weapons, so there's a surprisingly broad scope for trying out different tactics and some reward for replaying levels you've already beaten.  Placing a unit costs a certain amount of level cash, which is very limited. Replenishing ammunition for a unit also costs level cash, so on each level you need to balance the number of units you have against their ongoing ammo costs. Trained units cost the same as untrained ones, but giving better weapons to units increases both their base placement cost and their ammo restock cost, so it can actually be a good tactic to enter a mission with a low-priced weapon as well as a more powerful expensive one. You earn level cash throughout each mission: a certain amount for each alien you kill, with more powerful aliens awarding more cash on a kill. So far I've found that each level is basically won or lost in the first thirty seconds, as this is when money is tightest. After your initial placements you'll know if they're successful, in which case you'll kill all the aliens and have considerably more money to spend on more units and ammunition, or you won't kill the aliens, and you'll be out of ammo and lose the level.  Each level rewards you with campaign cash based on your performance. You even earn cash for failed missions, which is great; I hate feeling as though I've wasted quarter of an hour on a failed mission for no reward. Campaign cash has no bearing on the money you have available on each level. Instead, it can be used to unlock new troop types or train your existing troops, making them more powerful and unlocking skill points to spend on the skill tree for each unit type. Most of these skills are simply better range or damage, or more ammo, but some skills are new abilities, like the grenade launcher your automatic-weapon-wielding marines can acquire.  On some levels supply crates can be found, too. Shoot these (repeatedly -- they have a lot of hit points!) to gain a weapon on successful mission completion. You can also spend cash on supply crates between missions, if you have any to spare after purchasing and training your troops. The weapons from the crates are random, but the better the crate type the more likely you are to get a unique or legendary weapon.  The game includes 35 standard levels, each playable on four difficulty levels, as well as some survival missions, where your goal is to survive as many waves as possible. Each of the three basic difficulty levels on each mission rewards you a bronze, silver, or gold star, depending on your performance, with cash bonuses accompanying each. I've played for a little over three hours and I'm only about a third of the way through the standard missions so far and I've had to repeat some of them a few times to earn the gold star. I'm also nowhere near maxed out in upgrades for even one of the seven troop types, so there's a fair bit of game time here, particularly if you're an achievement hunter, as some of the included Steam achievements are pretty difficult.  [h1]PROS AND CONS[/h1] Pros: + Good advancement model, with troop training and skills as well as weapon improvements and upgrades + Clever game balance due to increased cost of placement and ammunition restocks for troops with better weapons + Mines, dynamite, and drones add another 'last-ditch' option + Fairly good graphics; easy-to-use interface + Automatic ammunition reload option is a useful addition + Quite a bit of game here + Steam achievements and trading cards  Cons: - Only seven types of troops - Not a lot of variation in alien types - Can get repetitive after an hour or two at a time, but easy to get back into again.  [h1]CONCLUSION[/h1] Alien Shooter TD is a solid addition to the relatively crowded tower defence genre. The game world is fairly uninspired, but the inclusion of clever balancing between unit, weapon, and ammunition costs, as well as weapon upgrades and skill trees, makes for plenty of improvements to keep you playing.   If you haven't played a TD game before then this one is a reasonable place to start, and if you have, then Alien Shooter TD is a pretty good place to get your fix.  [h1]70/100[/h1]  Note: I received this game for free for review purposes. This did not influence my review.
