Hearts of Iron IV is a game that I have spent a lot of time playing. I would definitely recommend this to anyone who is into in-depth strategy, complex military control, politics, management, and careful planning. I started playing this game when I saw a relative playing with it, and started off without any tutorials. Hearts of Iron IV, and most paradox games, have a large learning curve, and it can take several hours to even understand the basics.   I want to write this review, not only to highlight why I think this is a good game, but also to show you what to expect. I especially enjoy this game as I am a strategy buff, and this game represented a fun and extreme challenge for me to understand. As one of my favorite characteristics of this game, I will start off with the visuals. The graphics are very nice, and very adjustable for those who have old or less beefy PC's. The weather, when playing at a low speed, looks very appealing, and the day/night cycle is compatible with that of the Earth's. When it is night time on your half of the world, major cities illuminate the continent with a warm, bright, yellow. The cities stand out of the map as if you zoom in, and you can see 3D buildings, ranging from apartments and houses in cities, as well as factories, power plants, and dockyards in the countryside and coast. Military divisions are also 3D and visible, appearing as a soldier, tank, truck, or artillery piece, depending on the consistency of the division they represent. The uniform of the soldiers, and the make of the tank or artillery piece are dependent on the country they are controlled by. The oceans look very nice, and you can see the ocean's shelves where the depth changes from shallow and light, to deep and dark. You may also see ships cruising through, if a navy is deployed. As for the sky, you will often see rain and snow clouds, and sometimes, in the desert, sandstorms. (The weather, as in real life, can actually affect your units by attrition, visibility, temperature and more, however, soldiers can get used to certain climates, such as the blazing hot desert, or the freezing temperatures of snowy plains and forest). As for the air force, when planes are deployed in a province, you can actually see them in-game, with the paint, and design of the country they represent (German cross for Germany, RAF/French circles for France, Britain, and their subjects). Your planes, if in a combat zone with other planes, or enemy cities, can be seen dropping bombs, as well as fighting with one another, and crashing in flames and disappearing if hit. My favorite weather feature by far is the winter, where snow begins to coat the alps, and eventually most of the ground, (that is if you are in North America, Europe, or Southern South America). Mountainous terrain is also visible, such as the Ural mountains which can be seen coated in snow as a strip of alps throughout Western Siberia. Overall, very nice, and beautiful. That is, if you have a compatible PC.  Some other features I do enjoy apart from the graphics are things such as:  The statistics of a war. Being able to see the gargantuan toll of war, with people such as soldiers in the army, navy, and air force, openly reminds me of the selfish politics behind most wars, such as that of monarchies and fascists, and the immense loss of life in the thousands to even millions that is simply remarked to as a number to many generals and government officials.  The division template editor. It allows me to edit the companies and battalions of anything land-based, such as infantry, motorized troops, and tanks, also allowing me to add or remove support companies such as artillery, logistics, military police, maintenance, reconnaissance, radio signal, field hospitals, and much more. I am still learning about this part, as this is one of the hardest to understand and learn, but I have nailed most of the basics down.  The mods. The community often brings awesome and action packed mods that could probably count as DLC's. These mods, some of which have been made for several years by several people, are full of new content, ranging from alternate history, new technology, dates, national focuses, and more. Want to play in a world where the Central Powers won World War One? Want to play as Prussia in 1850 and form The German Empire? Want more starting dates than just 1936, and 1939? Want to try surviving as Germany in March, 1945? Want to play a mod that is full of memes and makes no realistic sense? The workshop has it all.  The research tab. The game includes several hundred things to research in the research tree, in several different categories. You can upgrade industrial speed and construction, research new guns, tanks, aircraft, and support companies. You can also research different doctrines, from the blitzkrieg, to mass assault. There are several game-changing technologies you can discover. Looking to win the war in the air? Try researching jet engines before other nations do, and watch as you start destroying several obsolete propeller aircraft with just a few powerful jets. Looking to design indestructible tanks? Try researching super-heavy tanks, such as the Maus (if you're Germany), and watch as your enemies can only scratch the paint with their guns. Looking to annihilate your enemy in general? Research nukes first, and watch as thousands of enemy soldiers and tanks are vaporized by the atomic explosion.   Now, I would like to explain to those considering the game, what to expect, as there is quite a lot of things to learn. If you first dive into the game, I would recommend you just generally start off by watching some youtube tutorials, as the in-game tutorial is less informative in my experience (although it still won't hurt to check it out). I started this game by just playing it without tutorials, and it took me several hours to get a simple understanding of the basics. If you get discouraged, just know that there is an extreme learning curve that everyone who has bought the game and frequently played it has had to go through. The game consists of several complex mechanics that I will now list: Political Decisions and Officials, Production, Trade, Logistics, Construction, Political Popularity, Research, Military Management, Stability, Recruitment, Division Template Designer, and there is still much more.   This is just an idea of how complex this game can get. Overall, Hearts of Iron IV has been a very fun game. I do not regret the many hours I have spent, and will spend playing this game, and am happy to have finally turned the learning curve. Would I recommend this to other strategy lovers? Yes, definitely. Is this game worth the money? For sure. Is this one of the top strategy games on steam? Most likely, although I will have to look at other titles before I can be sure.  Thanks paradox for the amazing game!

レトログラフィックなローグライクアクション。  非常にレトロな見た目だが、これは1984年に稼働していたドラゴンバスターをオマージュしているとのこと。  実際の動画 https://youtu.be/MXn4EHGxCPs と見比べるといかに似ているかわかるだろう。   反面、レトロなのは見た目だけでなく中身もレトロだった。  本作はRisk of Rainのように同じアイテムを複数入手して強くなるゲームだが、チュートリアルは必要最低限、アイテムも入手時に説明なし、アイテム一覧から見なければ効果がわからない。  アイテム一覧も方向キー長押しで移動が不可能、何度もその方向に連打する必要があるなどまさにレトロ。  2段ジャンプはかなり重力が強くて慣れるのにやや難しく、ダンジョン入り口の矢印方向は統一されておらず間違えて入ってしまうことも。  トップ画面ではハイスコアが表示されるものの、プレイ中に確認は不可能。   それらが良いか悪いかの判断は難しいところだが、少なくとももっとユーザビリティが良ければおすすめできるゲームになっていた。 内容自体は面白いと思うのだが、そこに至るまでの道のりが長いようにも思った。  ただしドラゴンバスターオマージュという意味では現時点でも成功しているだろう。   そういう意味では、レトロという意味で本作の評価に迷った点でもある。  古のアーケードゲームをプレイした方からすれば良いリスペクト作品だが、それらをプレイしていない新規ゲーマーからするとユーザビリティの悪い作品としか見えない。  単純にレトロという意味を長所と短所に伸ばして評価してるだけであり、かなり判断に迷った。   他にも一部steam実績が取れないなどの不具合もあり、現状ではおすすめしかねる（当環境では「カラフルシールド！」と「いちばん　やっかいなやつ」がsteam側で取得できなかった）  なお肝心のスクリーンショットに対応してないが、これは[url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1136790/announcements/detail/1589135317216057478]仕様上難しく実装が困難[/url]とのこと。   本作は[url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561197976326496/recommended/1136790/]他の方が述べられているように[/url]スルメゲーに近い作品のようだが、そこまで楽しめる前に断念してしまったのは私の力量不足に他ならず残念ならない。

＜このレビューはファーストインプレッションです＞  [h1]◆概要◆[/h1]  爽快感あるスタイリッシュ2Dアクション。  ソウルライク系のようにスタミナ消費で回避が可能だが、攻撃時にスタミナは減らない。 さらには雑魚は非常にのけぞりやすく、こちらの攻撃を連続ヒットさせる爽快感があって良かった。  防御によるダメージ軽減やジャストガードからのカウンターも可能であり、値段やボリュームもお手頃のため（後述の最適化不足を除けば）入門編として良いかもしれない。  難易度バランスも（少なくとも序盤は）ボスの攻撃動作はわかりやすいものが多く、ステータスを上げることもできるためそこまで理不尽な感じはしなかった。   [h1]◆最適化不足について◆[/h1]  一方で不満点だったのは最適化不足。  本作は戦闘面が素晴らしい反面、システム面やキーコンフィグ不可など荒が目立つように思えた。  ざっと挙げると  ・グラフィック設定がなく、デフォルトだとフルスクリーン固定（ただしAlt+エンターキーでウィンドウモード化可能） ・キーボードの場合、操作方法はWASDで移動、Jで攻撃（決定ボタン）、Kでガード（キャンセルボタン）、Lでジャンプ、Uでウルトラスキルとやや慣れている人が少ない配置 ・↑に加えてキーコンフィグなし。これはコントローラーの方も同じ  ・加えてゲーム内のボタン表記はゲームパッドの表記のみの様子。キーボード勢にとっては「右ボタンを押せ」と言われてもどうすることも出来ないため、上記操作方法を参考にされたい（一応スキップも可能）。 ・さらにはトップ画面から設定画面に入ると何故か止まる（スクリーンショットは撮影できたため、フリーズではなく処理が止まっている？）  そのため、まずは[u]プレイできるようになったら最速で設定画面を開いてキー配置を見る[/u]ことをおすすめする。   本作唯一の不満点がこの最適化不足であり、それを除けば全体的にまとまっているのが残念でならない。   [h1]◆戦闘面について◆[/h1]  戦闘面は雑魚は無双、ボスは攻撃を読んで回避なバランスだった。  雑魚はのけぞるためこちらの攻撃で無双しやすく、近くのオブジェクトを破壊してHP回復できるため、ほぼ全快の状況で挑みやすいため問題ないだろう。   一方ボス戦は一撃がかなり痛く、敵の攻撃を読むことが重要。  敵のAIはなぜかベルトスクロールアクションのように真横方向の敵を狙う攻撃ばかりが多かったため、上下方向にドッジロールすると楽に避けられる…というのが建前。  実際は攻撃動作キャンセル→ドッジロールには一瞬隙が入り、避け損なうとダメージを丸々受けるためなかなかリスキー（正確には攻撃動作終了後に発動）。  逆に防御も同様に攻撃動作終了後に発生するものの、ジャストガードでなくてもガード中に食らうことで被ダメージ軽減になるため、基本は敵に張り付いて適度に防御することになるだろう。   [h1]◆ボリュームについて◆[/h1]  定価が520円と非常に安いように、ボリュームも少し少なめ。  全部で4ダンジョン+ラストダンジョン、1ダンジョン内は道中+ボスのセットが5つの様子？  ステータスアップも5段階でMAX、装備することで効果を発揮するルーンも見た目以上に数が少なく、良くも悪くも値段相応だと言えた。  プレイアブルキャラは全部で3体存在し、使い勝手はいずれも違う。 特に魔女は通常攻撃連打で雑魚を完封できるほど。  残念ながらステータスアップはキャラごとに個別であり、前のダンジョン（あるいはエリア）には戻れないようなので注意が必要。   チャレンジではボスと再戦でき、高評価を狙うことも可能。   [h1]◆終わりに◆[/h1]  やはり現段階では最適化不足が足を引っ張っているように思え、タイトル画面で設定画面に入ると動作が止まる、よりによってチュートリアルで進行不能になりそう、そもそもトップ画面の決定ボタン（キーボードだとJキー）がわからないなど改善点は残っている。  一方でそれを超えれば爽快感と死の緊張感のある戦闘が待っており、値段相応なボリュームで非常に良かった。

[h1]◆概要◆[/h1]  巨漢の女の子が主人公の弾幕シューティング。  steamでは意外となかった肩幅がでかすぎるキャラのゲームであり、全体的に愛に満ち溢れていた。    [h1]◆ゲームシステムについて◆[/h1]  操作説明はストアページに書いてある通りだが、本作には低速移動のみのボタンが存在せず、実質チャージボタンが低速移動になっている。  一方でチャージショットと通常ショットは同時並用可能なため、特に不便さを感じなかった。  というよりチャージショットの威力がかなり高めであり、スペカ開幕に当てられるとゴリゴリ削ることが可能。   一般的な東方系シューティングとは異なり、パワーアップアイテムは触り続けることで連続してパワーが上昇。 これを利用してのスコア稼ぎも可能（ただしパワーアップアイテムも得点アイテムも上方に行っても自動収集はなし）。  パワーの上限は1000であり、ボム1発で250消費、ボムの効果も周囲の敵弾を消すだけ、パワーダウン後は目に見えてショットの威力が下がるためボムの乱射には気をつけたい。   また水色の敵弾はショットで打ち消すことが可能であり、これを利用した弾幕が飛んできたりも。    [h1]◆やりこみ要素について◆[/h1]  難易度イージーでクリアしたのみだが、全4ステージ、エンディング的にもエクストラなどはないと思われる。  難易度ハードで弾幕の種類が変わるのはもちろん、難易度ノーマルですらかなり弾幕の速度が速くなるため、あまり得意でない方はいきなり難易度イージーでも良いだろう。   肝心のスコアアタックについては[spoiler]会話画面で無限にチャージショットできてしまう[/spoiler]ためあまり意味はなさげ。  どちらかといえばタイムアタックが熱そうな。  2020/12/16追記： 不具合だったため修正される様子。   各難易度をクリアすることで難易度選択画面でクリアマークが付くが、個人的にはsteam実績も同時取得できればやりがいがあった。    [h1]◆終わりに◆[/h1]  ボリューム的にも控えめでサクッとクリアできる作品だが、非常にキャラ愛に溢れている作品だった。  エンディングはラフ画に近い感じだったが、逆にそのかげで背景でわちゃわちゃしていて非常に和んで良かった。  スペカの演出が格好良かったのも非常に良かった。   TCSTRIKERS「1」とあるように続編もリリースされている作品（[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1374410/TCSTRIKERS2/]2[/url]、[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1294170/TCSTRIKERS3//]3[/url]）であり、気になった方は購入してみても良いだろう。

[h1]      BATMAN ARKHAM CITY - O MELHOR JOGO DA SAGA [/h1]                                                                              [h1]                INTRODUÇÃO [/h1]  Batman Arkham City é o penúltimo jogo da saga, em questão da história, sendo também, sucessor de: Arkham Origins e Asylum.   Este é considerado por muitos, inclusive por mim, como o melhor jogo da saga. Arkham City não tem os melhores gráficos, nem o maior mapa muito menos o batmóvel, mas ele tem algo em especial que prende os jogadores, no caso, sua magnífica história, considerada pela grande maioria dos fãs como a melhor. A história principal conta com 3 vilões que vão aparecendo ao desenrolar da história.  2 deles são novidades e exclusividades para esse jogo e o outro é ninguém menos que o Joker (Coringa), o vilão mais conhecido do Batman.                                                                       [h1]    SINÓPSE [/h1] Hugo Strange, um ex diretor do Asilo Arkham e inteligente psiquiatra, que é obcecado pelo Batman, resolve aprisionar os maiores loucos, criminosos e qualquer pessoa que já tenha cometido algum delito em uma cidade chamada de Arkham City. Ele tem um plano do que fazer com todas essas pessoas. Ele é chamado de PROTOCOLO-10 e consiste em aniquilar todas essas pessoas. Para impedir a fuga e iniciar a matança, Hugo contratou uma equipe de militares treinados, a Tyger, que será mais um obstáculo para o Homem morcego. Hugo Strange não é alguém forte, pelo contrário, mas é uma pessoa extremamente inteligente e tem uma informação que pode ser usada como uma arma, ele é um dos poucos que sabe a verdadeira identidade do Batman.                                                                     [h1] Jogabilidade [/h1] É quase idêntica com os outros jogos da saga. Poucas coisas mudam. As novidades são novos e melhores apetrechos. O combate é mais cadenciado, em relação aos anteriores jogos. Principalmente em Arkham Origins, parece que o combate é um pouco mais rápido e parece que o tempo para perder o combo é maior. São pequenas mudanças que não alteram muito no jogo, mas dá para entender o motivo. A base da jogabilidade foi formada no primeiro jogo (ordem de lançamento) e agrada a grande maioria dos jogadores. Em cada jogo, ela vai ganhando pequenas mudanças e evoluindo.                                                                                   [h1]Pontos + - [/h1]   +História +Gameplay +Boss battles da campanha principal +Presença de novos personagens +Final épico +DLC. A DLC coloca o jogador em um conto após os eventos da história principal. Temos uma variação entre controlar o Batman e Robin. A gameplay dura por cerca de 1h e é bem completa, tendo até mesmo uma Boss Battle com a antagonista, a Arlequina.  -Mal otimização na versão de PC -Missões secundárias. Elas não são péssimas, mas deixavam muito a desejar. Todas usam uma mesma fórmula bem tosca, vou usar a missão do Victor Zsasz como exemplo. O jogador tem que ficar pela cidade esperando que ele ligue em um telefone e ir rastreando seu local de pouco em pouco tempo. Se não me engano, são mais de 5 ligações. Depois de rastrear seu local, vamos até lá, o acertamos com um golpe e fim.                                                                                  [h1]Conclusão [/h1] Se você procura um jogo do Batman mais focado em uma incrível narrativa cheia de mistérios, reviravoltas e um dos melhores desfechos da história dos jogos, Batman Arkham City é o jogo ideal. Além da narrativa, o game mantém toda a sua qualidade já vista em antecessores.   [quote=art] Protocol 10 will begin in 10 hours... [/quote]

之前7号在yuplay 57买的key，注册了一下b社平台绑定了steam然后好友帮忙激活的，然后进游戏只用连接上b社服务器就可以进入游戏了，我看好多人卡在登不上这个问题，b社官网直接可以直连，注册绑定一次steam就好（或者仅仅注册b社账号，steam版进游戏登陆注册的b社账号一样的），然后进游戏用一下加速基本可以连接上。   至于游戏内容，14号当晚就玩了一下。游戏三种模式，第一种是所有人在一个废土地图求生，第二种直接是官方给你的8人私服模式，但是需要每月会员，第三种还没看，是beta的吃鸡模式。怎么说，感觉一个人玩还是有点孤单的，还有游戏里有饱食度，和对水的需求这两种指标，会随着时间的流逝慢慢降低。这就意味着你要在废土不停的找食物和干净的水，这对于新手来说还是有点困难的。因为有些地方有很多蛮厉害的怪物（变种人mutant，僵尸zombies那些，包括被辐射变异的一些巨大生物，最不和谐的某些僵尸居然还有枪，而且成群结队，一个人打不过的–.–），需要类似玩生化危机那种模式绕路搜刮，不太建议新人上来就硬打，比较伤。然后接着说这个食物系统，就是吃东西一般都会增加辐射值（辐射值满了也会死），喝水最好喝纯水或者其他可乐，酒等饮料，但是这些商店卖的比较贵，污水会加辐射值，建议前期看到水管接点污水，然后到烹饪地方烧开水再喝，起码不会得病，但是还是在接水的时候会加辐射值。睡觉可以回复血量，一般用钱买消除辐射的药就行（后来发现双头牛奶可以降低25%辐射，那么就攒钱买图纸）。        前期不知道干什么，建议一边做任务一边搜刮，看到什么就捡，到工作台分解之后做几件护甲和一把枪，多余没有用的放到储藏箱或者找npc卖掉。这里感觉还是不科学的，大概是需要魅力值口才的缘故，捡来垃圾不管显示的定价是多少瓶盖基本都是只能卖npc一个瓶盖，然而比如一瓶酒（不加辐射值，解渴）居然都要30瓶盖，感觉太坑，还不如自己搜刮搜刮，野外遇到随机的动物敌人打死之后比如鼹鼠肉，建议不要直接吃，而是去烹饪锅制作，虽然也会加辐射值，但是起码得病概率降低很多..        由于只玩了3－4小时就来评价了，好多内容有待发掘，这游戏的精髓就是不停捡垃圾，里面的东西会自然刷新（除了你自己的储藏柜），最好有小伙伴一起，一个人确实有的时候力有未逮。这游戏画质还是非常好看的，各种光影，色彩，反正不比辐射4的色彩感差，效果还高于4，但是任务的存在感以及你作为从避难所里出来的一员感觉归属感太差，如果不是了解之前的作品的新人还是建议不要玩这个了。   总的来说，这游戏并不是一无是处，其实作为娱乐消遣还是蛮好的，除去连不上之外，还有上手比较难，游戏玩家相对比较少，个个都在大地图上有表示，（可能刚上steam人少或者进不去）。但是除了（新人出76避难所一把武器都不给你能信?单机版都还给），废土npc个个都是黑商之外，普通模式你不用担心玩家或者npc背刺你，你只要想办法再废土时间中找食物，想办法活下去。不需要额外花钱高级会员和饰品，其他没有花钱的地方，在这个程度上，其实还是比较符合末世生存类游戏，不恰当的拿来和dyinglight 比，除了不是动作不能攀爬跑酷，还增加了饮食系统之外，其他和这个游戏没有什么差别，没事就是跑跑图，看看风景，听听音乐，搜刮资源，做做任务打打怪，一定意义上的休闲游戏   说这么多还是希望有大佬加好友一起玩，我这小透明一个人玩太难了~！

I'm going to open this review with this statement. I played this game, not sure what to expect, especially since this is an RPG Maker game. But, so far... As of the writing of this review, it's not too bad. Certainly a far cry from a Game of the Year winner, but... It's pretty good for a dirt cheap game.  Gameplay is quite simple. Get your character within range to attack and hit the attack button until you need a healing item or your enemy is dead. The game's tutorial is fairly easy to grasp as well, since Alma seems to explain herself the game's mechanics.  Story is quite simple from what I've seen. You play as Alma, a female... I should probably say that I’m newcomer to the series and Half-Genie Hero is my first game in the franchise.  I liked the game, which seems strange considering my final vote on it – my final feelings lie somewhere in the middle, but Steam doesn’t have neutral score, so I cannot use this. The game certainly looks polished when you play it – characters look beautiful, music is fantastic and animation fluid. Game plays smoothly and responsively (usually, we will talk later about some forms...). The level design is good and most of the levels are blast to play. Transformation are fun and open a lot of new ways to move though levels, other power-ups and spells make fight interesting and give players a lot of options to dispatch enemies.  So far it seems like very nice platformer, doesn’t it? However, the longer you play, the more cracks start to show. There are only few (hub, five main and final) levels, which wouldn’t be a problem – game doesn’t really have to be very long to be good and leave nice impression, but you can see that creators saw short length of the game as big problem and were afraid that it seemed to short. Most of my problems stems from methods they applied to combat this problem.  - First, that five main levers? They are very interesting first time you play though them and nice second time, with some small changes in monster or trap placement. However, you better hope you will really like them, because you will be playing them over and over trying to find that missing upgrades necessary to progress your story. At this point I just cannot look at beautifully designed and interesting creepy factory level considering how many times I have to beat it. When you have to give players spell to skip parts of the world to get instantly to next level (you get that and this is immensely helpful, but still doesn’t  eliminate main problem) you really should think if amount of backtracking isn’t too big. At some point it just stop being fun (and I’m a completionist type of player) and start to seem like artificially padding the game’s length.  - Instant death traps spanning entire sublevels. Well, they are not exactly instant death (you only lose some energy after failing and are moved to the beginning of challenge), but they are rather long with no checkpoints in the middle. It wouldn’t be that bad, but they are designed for you to fail at least few times before you can play them from memory. Two of them remove most of your special skills and make you fall down slippery slope while jumping over chasm and avoiding barrels (don’t know, maybe it is series tradition? Doesn’t really seem fun), with some jumps timed in the way that you cannot really succeed on them without inhuman reflexes or precise knowledge coming from failing them before – and if you will, you will have to replay entire segment from the beginning.  Another one is “lava rising” type of the level – you need to climb tower while instant kill condition rise from the bottom. This is classic platformer design, however even in Ninja Gaiden series it was clear where you should jump – Shantae sublevel is long and have tons of blind ends, making you constantly fail until you progress to almost the end and can play sublevel from memory where you should move to avoid moving into blind end.  - These instant death trap type of sublevels? One of them comes just after final boss. It’s extremely fun to have do trial and error long gameplay segment when you have just won final fight and want to sit back and relax while story unfolds ;-)  - There is instant death sublevel build entirely on how unwieldy and full of inertia is one of the transformed Shantae’s forms. I know that controls of that form are bad, you don’t have to show me that so much ;-)   - Lots of upgrades seem like afterthought – for example, special power of bat transformation is used exactly once and only to get relic that allows another (not really useful for combat) almost optional form to attack.  - There is an upgrade late game (I think you get it for unlocking entire art gallery? Not sure) that gives you unlimited mana allowing for endless casts of spells. Doesn’t seem too bad, strong bonus for completionists, until you realize it means unlimited instant full life heals, unlimited healing items spawn and unlimited invulnerability bubble spell.  Because of that final level consist mainly of instant kill spikes, while final bosses are a joke.  - For the end – characters. They seem fun and interesting. They seem to know Shantae, but I have no idea how and why. If you don’t know them from previous installments, there is pretty much zero explanation who they are, how they know Shantae and why are they friends/enemies.  To sum up -  I enjoyed most of this game, at least until more annoying parts came up, killing my enjoyment each time. It is a very nice game and I hope there will be next game in the series that will polish problems this one is full of – but at this point, my opinion is a little more negative than positive (I would really like to be able to choose neutral opinion in Steam review options).

（通常・DLC共に全クリア済） （レビュー文の下の方に[b]問題SKIPのやり方・フルスクリーン解除の仕方[/b]の解説補足も追記）  囚われのウサギ君を救出するためにパズルを解いてアイテムを集めまくるポイントクリック型ゲーム。 通常版はマジシャンの部屋、DLCの「The Abyss」は何故か海の底が舞台になってます。 基本的に何をすれば先に進めるのかはノーヒントなので、とりあえず手探りで怪しい所をクリックし、 パズルが始められそうならそれを解いて報酬アイテムゲット、 何かが足りなくて始められないようなら他のところを廻ってそれっぽいアイテムを探す、という流れ。 たとえばジグソーパズルはテープで封がしてあるのでまず別の場所でカッターナイフを探す、といった感じ。 日本語非対応ですが英語は短いプロローグと中間デモ（どっちも一枚絵）くらいで、 ミニゲーム中は一切文章無いので必要無いです。 一部ミニゲームにあるヒントもイラストのみによる抽象的なもの（なので一見ちょっと分かりづらいものも）。  収録パズルの難易度はそこそこ。 中にはジグソーパズルや4ピース回転パズル、DLCのハンガリアンリングスなど多少面倒なものもあります。 （チェスの駒のパズルだけどうしてもルールがイマイチ理解できなかったので攻略動画でズルしてしまいました） 欠点といえばボリュームが少ないこと（通常版は2時間程度、DLC含めても4時間ほどで全クリア可能）。 エンディングも救出されたウサギ君が喜んでる「YOU WIN!」の一枚絵のみの簡素なもの。 ただしその分価格も安めなので値段相応と言えるかも。セールで￥49+￥98で購入しましたが充分楽しめました。 実績も各パズル攻略で1つずつという感じなので全クリア（＋最後に後述のスキップ実績）するだけで簡単にコンプできます。  [h1]補足[/h1] スキップ機能も一応存在しますが、普通にSKIPボタンをクリックするだけだと [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=530809831#810775]コミュニティガイドのスキップ方法解説ページ[/url]に飛ばされてしまいます。 上記のページにも反転で書いてありますが、実際にスキップするには[spoiler]ALTキーを押しながらSKIPボタンを押す[/spoiler]という操作が必要です。 自分の環境だとフルスクリーン状態でスキップボタンを普通に押すだけだとゲームに復帰できなくなる状況になったので注意。 なおスキップするとスキップ実績が付きますが、それ以降他の実績が解除されなくなる（リセットが必要）らしいので注意。 実績コンプ目当てにスキップする場合は全クリア後がオススメ。  [b]デフォルトではフルスクリーン強制[/b]で、通常はウィンドウモードへの切り替えは不可能ですが、 [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=420025259]コミュニティガイドのこちらのページで解説されている[/url]通りに ライブラリからこのゲームのプロパティを開いて一般→「起動オプションを設定」ボタンを開き、 「1920 1080 false」のように解像度を併記してコマンドを入れておくとウィンドウモードで起動できます。 数字は「1600 900 false」など環境に合わせてお好みで。

[code]感谢开发者与 3DM 独立游戏鉴赏家赠送的游戏。 若喜欢本篇评测，可点击关注：[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/32340435/]3DM 独立游戏鉴赏家[/url][/code]  《Tower Hunter: Erza's Trial 魔塔猎人》一个融合了 rpg，roguelike 元素的 2d 动作游戏。  《死亡细胞》作为近年最优秀的 2d 肉鸽动作游戏，我不得不将《魔塔猎人》和前者作比较，毕竟两者各个方面的相似度都太高。《魔塔猎人》有着和《死亡细胞》类似的死亡处罚机制和地图机制。  游戏名叫《魔塔猎人》，但其实地图并不像高塔一样延伸向上，更像横版地牢式探险。而《死亡细胞》里的钟楼，堡垒，地图构造无一不是符合其名字所指的。《魔塔猎人》并没有做出一种高塔式的地图特色。  上面写的并不是打差评、不推荐的原因，作为动作类游戏，手感才是最重要的，但很遗憾《魔塔猎人》在这方面乏善可陈。游戏连招很多，技能也很丰富，可以说有个手柄会有非常好的游戏体验。不过还有很多影响体验的地方。  跳跃太慢易被攻击，某些技能释放前摇太慢伤害又不够，根本不实用。钥匙不是自动收集，需要按 r 键才能拿到，谁会不要钥匙呢？  游戏符文没升级起来，伤害不够，全是花拳绣腿，一个怪要打几套——游戏节奏太慢。加上宝石升级系统，每个物品或技能还要分 5 次升，真是内容不够等级来凑。武器符文平衡有待考量，打得好不如武器符文捡的好。  前些天更新的换装系统着实让我这种绅士开心了一番。吊带裤，黑丝袜，兔女郎...总有好这口的，爆装破衣指日可待？从最开始的小镇还有开头一闪而过的剧情可以看出作者的宏图壮志。不过还请作者不要忘记这个游戏的原本分类。如果想要两开花的话，希望能够把动作游戏的本行做好。  对了恶魔萝莉在哪？关卡打通了没找到。

Бесспорно, вселенная первых двух частей Bioshock по своему уникальна. И если первая часть очень удачно раскрывает перед нами специфику Восторга, рассказывает о его загадках и его истории, впервые погружает в его атмосферу, то вторая часть... ну да, она как бы все это сохраняет, и даже начало игры весьма интригующе играет на чувствах игроков, сразу задавая вектор направления сюжета, но вся основная часть игры вплоть до кульминации - скучна и однообразна.   Несмотря на то, что графику знатно допилили, да и идея игры за большого папочку интересна по определению, спустя пару часов игры складывается ощущение, что проходишь какой-то второстепенный однообразный квест. 1/3 игры можно просто вырезать и ничего особо не поменяется.   Зато все кардинально изменяется, когда история игры близиться к кульминации. Игра вновь захватывает, стандартные скучные стычки преобразуются в стремительный бой с разными противниками, интерес к сюжету вспыхивает с новой силой. Концовка ничуть не разочаровывает, к тому же, присутствует целых 6 ее вариантов, зависят они от вашей гуманности по отношению к маленьким сестричками и ключевым персонажам.   Вывод напрашивается противоречивый, но точно не отрицательный.  [b]7/10 [/b]

《NEOVERSE》是一款rougelike元素的卡牌冒险游戏，玩家扮演一名在各个时空世界进行冒险的冒险者，通过收集卡牌，从而击败更强大的boss。   游戏类型类似于我在手机上曾经玩过的一款游戏《魔女之夜》，也是通过收集不同的卡牌，集成相应的卡组，从而打出大量的伤害。游戏目前有三个角色，分别是：特工娜雅，圣骑士克莱拉，召唤师海伦娜。除了雅娜以外，其他两个角色都需要在通过一定关卡后才能解锁。  每个角色在最开始时都能够选择不同的卡牌路线，比如雅娜可以选择射击跟辐射等路线。但不同的路线在前期能够达成的战斗力相差较大，比如雅娜的射击路线，在开始几个回合时，你可能连boss的防御都打破不了，而boss一下就能打掉你非常多的血量。但如果你选择辐射路线，虽然每回合开始时可能没什么伤害，但只要坚持多几个回合，由于其辐射层数可以叠加，且每回合降低的层数不多，你就可以在后期打出远超射击卡组的伤害。  游戏目前处于EA阶段，可能也因此其游戏难度的把握做得并不是特别好。在前期，玩家很难通过自己的卡组通关所有三层关卡，可能在通关一两层之后就已经无力为继了，特别是抽到的卡牌组成的卡组并不是特别强大的时候，这种感觉尤为明显。  游戏在每回合都有可能遇到一些“奇遇”，这些有的是商店，有的是事件，有的是实验室。这些都能在不同程度上给予玩家一些帮助，比如玩家的血量在没有拿到补血卡组之前，只能在实验室里补给，卡牌的升级也得靠实验室，等等。  虽然游戏有着一定难度上的不合理，但在其的确非常有趣，与杀戮尖塔这种2d不同的精美3d建模，丰富有趣的卡牌，都是他的亮点之一，如果你喜欢爬塔类游戏，想看漂亮小姐姐，那它的确是你不可多得的良选。   [quote]欢迎加入[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/HY_Master]黄油大师[/url]，一同挖掘好玩的游戏吧~ 欢迎关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/33741419/]黄油大师鉴赏家[/url]，查看趣味性评测 喜欢这篇评论，可顺便点个赞，让更多人能够看到！[/quote]

《迷雾之夏》作为一款由国内制作开发的文字冒险解谜游戏，游戏的开场非常老套，荒郊野岭的别墅，突如其来的大雨，坍塌的道路，孤岛一般的场所，再加上过夜必死人的设定，一股传统推理小说的氛围扑面而来，所以最开始我对本作能玩出什么花样抱着一定怀疑的态度，但我在体验之后发现游戏还是蛮有意思的，首先是解谜方面，游戏的解谜难度中等，适合像我一样的休闲玩家体验。其次，游戏的人物和配音都在水准之上，虽然人物身体莫名有点宽，其余还算可以，但配音合格在国内作品中已经是非常难得的了，好的配音能够给赋予一个角色灵魂可不是开玩笑的。总之，作为一款解谜游戏而言本作完全合格，再加上不算非常高的价格，推荐喜欢解谜类型游戏的玩家体验。  [quote] 我的游戏真的有那么好玩吗? 关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/34823631/]鉴赏家[/url],这是你从未体验过的船新版本~ [/quote]

I anticipated buying this program for a while, thinking it truly was -draw silhouette, get said shape-. But it's one of those things that really seems better before you buy it, here's pretty much every thing you'll notice:  1- it won't ease your workflow, unless somehow you only ever need models of onions and peanuts. 2- the sculpting tools (section) are.. decent, but you'll always feel the need to finish the model in another program, looks at best 2003ish. 3- you will never be able to 'quick draw organic shapes' as it shows in the trailer. 4- you cannot turn a sketch into primitives, as it implies in the trailer. 5- only possesses about two unique features, the curve-object feature (remember, not silhouette, curve-object: onions and peanuts) and a tool to reshape the curves, useful only with the 'blob' object option. Again 'decent', but not amazing nor particularly a great addition to anyone's workflow in its current form. 6- the more you make an object complex, the more of a mess your topology will be, a not ideal yet somewhat normal consequence but: 7- you'll never be able to use what you create in this software for animating purposes (in other programs), unless you plan to spend weeks fixing topology, just cause you decided to use curvy3d. At that point, the object may as well be said to have been made in other software, and really, if you'd just made it in another program to start with you may not have run into this problem at all.  Mind you, you won't get refunds if you dare exceed two hours, even if you've been refunded other things you've used for more than two hours in the past. If you do, know that steam loves you.  So don't use it for that long. Or better yet, don't buy it at all.

O game é extremamente divertido tanto sozinho ou com os amigos, estão presentes os seguintes modos de jogo: Mata-mata, Corrida Armada, Demolição, Casual e Competitivo, é muito fácil encontrar partidas em qualquer um deles, geralmente leva apenas alguns segundos.  Os gráficos de CS GO pelo menos particularmente falando são bem bonitos e me agradam bastante, o game não é tão pesado e não exige um PC da Nasa, até mesmo para ser jogado com tudo no máximo. Os bots do game continuam estúpidos como sempre, é muito fácil ver eles parados, tentando entrar em alguma parede, descendo tiro como se não houvesse o amanhã ou presos em algum lugar, mas ainda sim estão bem mais “inteligentes” que os bots das versões anteriores. Existem coisas que decepcionam bastante no game, particularmente falando oque mas me incomoda é a comunidade brasileira que vive estragando o game, o que tem de gente escrota, mal educada e que vive de “mimimi” por qualquer coisa é um saco! A coisa mais fácil que tem é iniciar uma discussão com alguma babaca durante uma partida, sempre tem um para atrapalhar sua experiência de jogo. Já os cheaters não são tão comuns assim(apesar que com o tempo esta aumentando muito mesmo), ter tem, isso infelizmente é fato, a Valve tenta controlar mas nem sempre consegue e isso é um erro! No fim Counter-Strike Global Offensive é um jogo que eu recomendo muito, para quem é fã do clássico o game é indispensável e para quem é fã de FPS CS GO é uma ótima aposta, o game tem sim seus problemas mas não deixa de continuar sendo aquele CS maroto com os amigos que é sempre muito divertido e que faz e vai fazer você perder horas e horas jogando, xingando, sorrindo e se divertindo.
Sem perder a fidelidade da história do cinema e atrelando a boa jogabilidade esse é um dos melhores games de sobrevivência...

This is a simple racing/shooting hybrid based on classic games like Atari's Badlands (arcade) and Super NES games RPM Racing (Radical Psycho Machines), Rock 'N' Roll Racing and, more recently, Death Rally that's about finishing first while blowing up other racers. There really isn't too much content yet (only 4 tracks with some variations and 4 playable vehicles at the start) but it's fun and-in single player mode-challenging, but it's much more fun if you've got friends to play with. Not the kiddies though, as there is some NSFW language (occasional F-bombs). It looks good with a nice metal soundtrack and controls are surprisingly realistic, you can't just go all out around corners or you might roll over, let alone go off track. While I'm hoping there will be more content either added or unlocked as I play through, it's decent for the price and has the makings of a good party game. Just a slight thumbs up so far based mainly on single player and seemingly light amount of content/variety but if you like this type of game then it's a fine pickup at a good price.

I'm a scuba diver and just sitting at my pc playing this gave me the same sense of wonder at how stunning the natural world is, and the part we may have to play in keeping it that way. This game should be enjoyed at a slow pace, and is such a welcome break from the real world.  The incredible chapter including [spoiler] the prehistoric life [/spoiler] was an awesome element. TL;DR: It could use some tuning up and a lot of the horror isn't expanded upon as much as I'd like it to, but it's a demo, so, I guess give it a shot if you want to. 5/10 | 2/5 stars | 2/4      As interesting as it is, it could definitely use some more context clues to inform the player of what they're supposed to be doing. A task-list or something could definitely help, because I spent, literally, 30 of my 40 something minutes playing just walking around and trying to figure out what to do. That being said, it wasn't particularly scary. That's not to say it wasn't tense, or maybe it's just my own resilience to horror, but the best part of the game was the last few minutes. The slow burn wasn't exactly slow, or a burn, as a majority of your time playing will be purely spent walking around a static room, tapping on doors. The intended effect, that I imagine the full game will inevitably bring, is one of truly maddening death-by-a-thousand-cuts style of horror, where little things will eventually pile up and become overwhelming, or, like the outro to this demo, oppressively tense and powerful in it's presentation. I would very much like to play, and then re-review this game when it comes out in it's entirety, but as this is only the demo, I'm gonna have to say that I think, if you aren't one to fall for jump-scares or pseudo-atmospheric horror, you may as well skip it until the full game releases, where I feel that the developer will deliver something truly interesting, at the least.

This is a 'Yes, But' review - there are some MAJOR issues with this game which I will discuss below,  but the combination of the game's atmosphere, concept, and fantastically detailed gameplay make this worth at least one long play session. But... I think for most players, only one long play session.  ... So, to get into the meat of it.   I don't really think this game knows what it wants to be.  Why do I say that?  On the one hand it's a slow, thoughtful big picture strategic experience. On the other, it doesn't give you the tools you need to be slow and thoughtful - it gives you the tools you need to be arcadey and detail oriented.   The trouble is, every individual piece of this game is fantastic, but it's when they all get added together that something gets lost.  An example - scouting.  In this game, scouting involves using a camera, either on your carrier or an aircraft, to literally tag each and every individual enemy on an island. Until you do that, you can't really engage the enemy.  The first few times? This is brilliant, immersive. You get to know what's out there, you learn the terrain you'll be fighting over before you get there, everything's great. It also serves to give you time to plan out how you'll deal with the island, or call for support assets - like artillery or cruise missiles - to make initial strikes.  The dozenth time waiting around while you ping every single set of headlights on an island in the middle of the night it's not merely a chore, it becomes a hindrance. You already have your plan - you've invaded a dozen islands just like this one, after all. You just need to know where the specifics are - where's the airfield to dump a cruise missile on, where are the turrets to use artillery on, etcetera. But you can't act on it, you have to find every individual enemy on that island or when it comes time to call in a missile or send an amphibious tank after it, you won't be able to target it for an attack command.  This pitch perfect individual system becomes an active hindrance later in the game - a non-optional halt to the rest of the gameplay.  The weapons systems are diverse and interesting, but some of them just... don't work when handed to the AI. I can't count the number of times my Mantas actually put their light bombs on target, because they effectively never did - unless I piloted the bombers myself, removing myself from the big picture entirely.  So maybe the game isn't a slow paced strategic experience - maybe it's twitch and arcadey. But then we should be putting in a plan of action that all units can participate in while we just grab on e and fly around, right? Except the command system is detailed - you move waypoints on a map for each vehicle where you want it, put in commands - often you have to specifically target a specific vehicle ahead of time. So juggling all these plans becomes onerous - you can't just use a standard RTS style 'attack move' command on an aircraft or tank and be sure it'll work while you go in guns blazing with another platform.  Yet, that finicky command system lets you do some very detailed things - I'd set up patrol loops where my plane circled the enemy island, with brief pauses to fire missiles at specific targets, or set it up so that four helicopters would hold off at ten kilometers then at my go-code they'd swoop in and fire all their missiles in a single huge barrage...  Which was easy for one helicopter, but doing it for the second, the third, the fourth, meant repeating the exact complex sequence of orders to achieve it.  So the game... isn't quite sure if it wants you to be able to do that. Isn't quite sure if it wants you to have complex plans, or if it wants you to go in guns blazing. Isn't sure if it wants you to enjoy the atmospheric experience of scouting an island, or if it wants you to be forced into a repetetive chore.   There's ways around all this... (a more flexible orders system, with copy-paste orders and the ability to delay vehicle launches until a given go-code, a scouting drone that does all the scouting for you, just slower than you would manually, to preserve the effectiveness of doing it yourself, an attack-move order that works for all aircraft, an attack-move order that has vehicles properly engage the enemy instead of breezing by) ... but none of them have been taken.  So, what IS this game?  It's an amazing simulation where almost every switch you can see on your bridge matters - actually does something. It's atmospheric as all hell, from the groans of your carrier in a storm to being able to watch individual aircraft get put on the carrier lift and sent out. Some surprisingly good lore in voice-over transmissions combined with a thrilling campaign end-game of chasing down the enemy carrier to try and kill it make for an experience I won't forget in a hurry.  But... it's also not an experience I'm all that eager to replay in a hurry, either. Which is a pity, because with a bit more quality of life and direction, making the moment-to-moment gameplay more of a pleasure, this would be an easy winner for me. And when I say this game isn't a pleasure, at times, moment-to-moment? I'm not talking about spending minutes in travel and waiting for cruise missiles to hit - I'm talking about being unable to send out more than one cruise missile at a time while keeping guidance, I'm talking about accidentally losing almost all your ground units and being forced to either give up the whole game and restart or struggle with some very janky methods to clear an island, I'm talking about repeating the same set of orders five times to get helicopters to launch enough salvos of IR missiles to finally break an island's defence.  So. This one? It's absolutely worth playing, once. Maybe on a weekend you can dedicate to just one game. Keep some podcasts or youtube on the side for company during travel. Be astounded at a game environment that does absolutely everything right. Be flexible - there's a lot to criticise fairly in this game - and keep your expectations relatively low, and you'll keep finding great reasons to be surprised in a super positive way. But I think if you approach this expecting something as smooth and clean as a fighter plane's underbelly, where absolutely everything's easy and smooth to use, you could come out of this bitterly disappointed.

They warn you about the game being in early access, but honestly, the issues are so few and far between that there's no need. The game is solid, even in multiplayer.  You achieve basic automation quickly enough to keep the tedium down (unless you don't automate anything and have to manually craft everything - this is faster than automated processes, for the most part, but there's so many other useful things you could be doing that you'll just end up holding yourself back). This helps keep the repetitive gameplay loop feel more fresh.  Tearing down your factory to rebuild it better is also much less of a chore than you initially expect. You get 100% of your resources back, and all items in each building (or on the conveyors) will be added directly to your inventory (or to a box on the ground if your inventory is full).  So far, the tractors are a little janky, but not bad enough to do much more than mention it. At the moment, it seems best to keep one tractor per vehicle bay, as their pathing seems to sometimes collide/conflict (even when the vehicles don't), causing them to stop.  This game is BEST played with at least one other human being. I got it back when it first released on Epic and played for a couple days before it got a bit too tedious (also, there wasn't nearly as much in the game at that point as there is now - no trains, tractors, etc, IIRC), but playing with a second person has completely changed that. During the startup, I gathered resources and moved through milestones while my friend (new to the game) got to fully explore the crafting/automation tools as they came in and without much interruption. Day one got us up to the second Steel milestone, day two was a move and complete overhaul of the factory, and day three was exploration and steel production. We still haven't done the second Space Elevator milestone, but we basically can whenever we feel like it at this point.

Warhammer Dawn of War 2: Retribution continues the Dawn of War 2 game series by adding a really shit campaign that can be played as any of six different races, the only thing changing in them is sometimes slightly different encounters/factions to fight against and some of the dialogue to occasionally give a weak reason as to why the stuff and things are happening here. Guys, this is a 2D SNES  game that is 3 years old, yet they are trying to sell it for $60.  These greedy developers just try to milk off nostalgic SNES gamers that remember the old great era of JRPGs.  That's what I thought prior to purchasing this game several days ago.  I held off on buying this game for years because of that.  $60 is an absolutely absurd price to pay for an RPG these days.    I was missing out on so much by holding out, because this game is one of the best RPGs I have ever played and is on par with Chrono Trigger, Super Mario RPG, and any final fantasy game.   First of all, the most underrated part of any RPG is always music and art.  The music is very good for the theme of the game and really gives you the feeling of hitting the road, toward your next town to meet your newest sidekick or completing another part of a character's questline.  The music won't blow you away, but there's some memorable tracks such as the desert theme and the boss themes.  It does its job in setting the mood and mindset of whatever you're doing.  The graphics also give you that road like feeling.  The entire overworld is you traveling on mostly well defined paths, with the occasional town, cave, or treasure to find.  The game encourages you to pay attention as you explore, either showing you a new side path, or giving you a glimpse of a hidden chest that you have to find your way to.  The latter is especially true in the dungeons.  The dungeons are small, but densely packed with these side paths to lucrative treasures, some very difficult to find pathways toward.  The innovative story of this game is what hits this game out of the park.  This game has 8 main characters, and each has a story long enough to be an RPG game in its own right, as the game is about 100 hours for full completion.  The character's personalities differ wildly, from priestesses to temptresses, knights, merchants, etc... and each get fully developed with main character treatment.    There are only a couple of small weaknesses in the game.  First of all, there's no auto XP, so if you want to use all of your characters you will have to grind a little bit, though it's not extreme because the XP curve makes it very easy for low level characters to catch up.  The second thing is that because the game is designed around 8 main characters, they don't have much to say to each other.  Most of their stories are individually played out with their towns and their main quest missions.  I don't have a problem with this, but you don't get relationships developing between characters save for a handful of spots where there is some basic banter.    The balance of this game is it's one of the best RPG games I have ever played.  This game is worth every bit of $60.  I wasn't going to pay $60 because I didn't trust it, and I got it on a sale, but if you see it for $60 and there's no sign of a sale, get it.  If you are an RPG fan this will blow you away compared to other games released today.

A Masterclass in Ambiguity: Inside  Inside, developed by Playdead and released on Steam, is an unequivocal triumph in the world of video games. A spiritual successor to the acclaimed Limbo, Inside continues the tradition of crafting a haunting, atmospheric puzzle platformer that leaves an indelible mark on the player.  The beauty of Inside lies in its seamless blending of the visual and auditory aspects to craft a narrative without uttering a single word. The stark, oppressive world is rendered in a way that the minimalist art style paradoxically teems with detail and story. The muted color palette and meticulously crafted visuals convey a depth of emotion that few games manage to capture.  The atmospheric sound design deserves equal praise, reinforcing the narrative elements with the ebb and flow of ambient sounds that pull players deeper into the game's universe. The music is not just a complement to the visuals, but an equal partner in storytelling.   The game's greatest strength, however, lies in its ambiguous narrative. It refuses to spoon-feed the player, instead opting for a cryptic story that inspires discussions and theories. It's a brave choice that enhances the game's lasting appeal and reinforces the unsettling, dystopian world the game depicts.  Excited to see Playdead's next game and take all the time you need to develop the next game!

The characters and story are great. The game play is superb. The open world is limited but the experiences of that limited set of destinations avoids the redundancy of games like the original Assassins Creed where you could go places but soon learned it was just monotony and redundancy in them. This isn't Skyrim where you get lost in side quests and occupy 80-100 hours of your life out in the hills. It feels more like the experience of Mass Effect, localized and relevant worlds to explore. (Follow [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/42150626-Jarl%2527s-Game-Treasury/]my curator[/url] for more reviews like this)  Dreams in the Witch House is a great adventure game, and one of the best Lovecraftian games I ever played.  It captures the vibe of Lovecraft perfectly: a gloomy New England town, a strange mystery that begins as bad dreams but slowly reveals itself to be far more sinister as you dive deeper into the occult. Dark, dreary, foreboding. A slow buildup that keeps throwing mysteries at you. Perfect pacing for a Lovecraft-themed game. I won't spoil the story, so let it suffice to say that it's very close to its source of inspiration. Lovecraft himself would have approved of this.  Gameplay is a little different from your usual point & click adventure fare, but it works. There are a few classic item combination puzzles, but they're rather simple. The real meat of the game is managing your time as a student at Arkham, and balancing your needs with your desire to figure out the mystery. You have to eat and sleep, and you can get sick from rain or cold unless you purchase the proper clothes to withstand bad weather. Money is always tight, and some puzzles require you to purchase certain items. Learning more about the occult takes time, but you also need to study for your exams. It's a delicate balance.  And while you are trying to get your life together, you keep having weird dreams that drip-feed you clues about what's really going on... how and when to investigate things further is up to you. The game is entirely non-linear and driven by your own actions. You can even choose to completely ignore everything, but that will lead - of course - to a bad ending!  Absolutely great adventure game that really makes you feel like you're slowly unraveling a mystery. Highly recommended.

An enjoyable, but ultimately grindy and repetitive experience. In contrast to most games, my 90+ hour playtime does not equate with deeper investment. Quite the contrary; the more I played Portia, the less I liked it. My biggest issue with the game is that production takes an *incredible* amount of time. What is fun at first quickly turns to dread when later blueprints require dozens of parts, themselves each requiring slow-to-process materials, which must be individually produced on expensive machines. Again, all this would be fine under different circumstances but the time gating slows down the pace far too much.  The combat is serviceable. The gathering resources is enjoyable, and the actual assembly of larger items is quite satisfying. The character design is simple but distinct, and the minigames are enjoyable enough. It's just the massive time wall that comes between you and any serious progression.  Overall I'd give a 'maybe' if I could. It is a pretty, charming game that only really begins to show its rough edges once you've dug into the real meat of the experience. Your enjoyment of Portia will really come down to how much you are invested in the characters, and how high your tolerance for grinding is.

Form a boy band and save the world!  This is a short review to recommend FF15 after my first playthrough on PS4.  FF15 offers a huge open world to explore, with some of the most beautiful views, and plenty of hidden secrets to unlock.  Even after beating the campaign your journey has only just begun. There are bonus challenges and dungeons that are far harder than anything you encountered during the story, and it's all new content, not just recycled NG+ type difficulty.  I highly recommend this game if you're a fan of Kingdom Hearts, as I believe the combat was designed by the same team.  If you're a oldschool FF fan, I can understand how this game might not initially be for you, but if you give it a chance, immerse yourself in to the game world, and listen as your party members squabble and talk your ear off, it could grow on you too.  Combat offers a multitude of strategy and unique personal playstyle if you take the time to learn how the weapons work, how to tag team with Cross-links, and how to exploit enemy weaknesses with spells and damage types. Don't forget to upgrade your skill tree in the Ascension system! If you don't upgrade you skills, the game feels like all you do is just hold down a single button to attack, just like Kingdom Hearts, so make sure you're investing your skill points in to the moves you want to enhance and you will slowly master the combat system over time!

This game is quite charming. You get the item randomization of games like Risk of Rain, mixed with the graphics of SNES or GBA era Castlevania, and more enemies on screen than Dynasty Warriors, What's not to like?  Gameplay consists of choosing a character that will change your starting weapon and give you a unique passive, like extra projectiles or shorter cooldowns; selecting a map you want to run; and then attempting to survive for 30 minutes while getting xp for killing enemies which after leveling-up lets you pick a single item or weapon to equip/upgrade for that run only. After the 30 minutes is up the game will introduce a mechanic that generally forces your run to end, so don't feel bad when you see that game over screen!  I hope the dev continues to add more items and characters, because after only 13 hours I'm almost out of achievements and I already generally know how all the item combinations will play out as there are only 9 weapons total (sort of) but you get to have 6 equipped every run. So there isn't really going to be a super unique combination of items, at least not until they finish all of the item evolutions.  If you like roguelites, wave survival, castlevania (art), and just generally killing endless hordes of enemies for 30 minutes at a time, go buy this game now, it's only $3!

From your headquarter/base/town you decide what to bring into the next mission, that means which units, artifacts, two choices for your hero's stats and abilitys, and then you see three challenges for the mission. They can be like, don't use this unit in the whole mission or don't pick this power when leveling, therefore a ¨challenge¨ if you complete one, two or all three you get a reward specific for each challenge.  When you have taken a mission, theres a food system, it means that every round takes 1 food, therefore making your turns and what you do very strategic. What i did was scout out the map and planning a route i wanna take and monsters i wanna beat first and so on, then reloading (save scum kinda idk) to the start of the mission and then do the route i had planned. Making sure that i wouldn't have enough food (you can find food throughout the mission)  So before heading into combat, theres taverns (idk if they are called taverns ingame) that has three units in them that costs resources that you get throughout the mission, having two of the same unit makes you able to merge them, into a stronger version of the unit. Theres also three different options for ending and starting the next round, you have like, get 2 extra moves next round, get two extra resources next round or get this buff next round. So depending on what you wanna do the next round/turn you have three options, if its a turn where you pick up stuff only, you might not want the buff, but if you wanna fight the next turn you might want to.  So in combat your units have shields and so do your enemy. The shields are a way to make it more strategic in my opinion because it gives you a chance to get out of combat without having to refill your units like in HOMM, because how it works is that if you only get damaged your shield number your unit is totally fine, its when your units shield gets destroyed and their health gets hit, which meaning after battle you have to do turns/rounds to refill their health, if i recall correctly tho the shield gets refill insta after battle. The worst scenerio is when your units gets killed, because then you lose the unit of course, and that means that the high cost of resources you used to buy them now are lost, so you really don't wanna lose a unit, it makes the mission harder because you are weaker and have lost the resources you used on that unit. Also why i said i feel it makes combat more strategic because you gonna do everything in your power to make sure that you get the best result.  Also the mana system, i haven't sat down and learn very much about it, but so far it seems that it refills in turns, could be wrong. But also your units have unique powers, but those powers cost from your mana, but could turn the tides in your favour.  So i bought the game because i really like HOMM, and they do have some similars aspects, but i could also see that a HOMM player would not like the game, but i could also see if they wanted something similar thats a breath of fresh air that they would enjoy it. But again its not HOMM, and thats a good thing, they have decided to make a unique take on the genre and it works very well.

Interesting concept, but flawed execution. The writing should have been done by real writers, as its about as subtle as a sledgehammer driving a tack through a wall, but I'm glad it's there. This is the only stock sim game that is wrapped around any kind of narrative, to my knowledge (aside from Wall Street Kid on OG Nintendo). The game is very, very light on realism, as all you can do is buy at current price and short at current price. The markets are quite reliably predictable, as well. If you want something like this but that feels somewhat more like a sim and is more difficult and complex, check out 'wall street raider' or 'speculator' by roninsoft.   There's some ludo-narrative dissonance here. Even without 'cheating', (which the game 'suggests' to you constantly, gotta love that subtle writing), the core gameplay loop is ridiculously easy. I won't describe it here, but the trade feed is all you need to pay attention to.  The problem with this is that even if you try to be a good trader and not intentionally manipulate anything, you will still be treated as if you are Bernie Madoff. Nobody likes illusion of choice. Everyone wants to feel as if their choices matter in a game. I get why they do this though, it's to hammer home their message that the financial industry is cartoonishly evil.. These kinds of messages are far more effective when better written though. I would have enjoyed this game much more from a role playing standpoint if it was nearly impossible to make money the traditional way, but cheating allowed you to win big bucks. I also got wrapped up in an endless mode without realizing it for a while, which was annoying, but they fixed that today according to patch notes.   The most annoying part though is a bug that will sometimes sell and buy your stocks in ridiculously small increments, per 'tick'. Other times, the full amount will post in one tick, as you would expect. This is more apparent later in the game, during the 'vice president' sections (math errors using larger numbers I guess?). If I have 900m, sometimes the game will sell or buy only a few million per 'tick'. This means you're completely helpless if an event occurs that tanks the stock, as you're not able to sell off quickly enough to not lose a fortune. Still, this isn't much of a problem since it's so easy to make money.   In short, I love the concept of a stock trading game wrapped up in a narrative, and it's a topical game given the whole GME/dogecoin etc... thing, but the writing leaves much to be desired. Still, it was worth the money for the novelty of it.

Real Talk   This game is great for a battle royal game easily worth the 20 dollars if you are on the fence grab it. It plays similar to Apex Legends but with more focus on melee. and unique abilities to literally parkour over anything and grapple on to anything even players.  Pro: Great game overall, graphics, game play, Parkour, weapons, abilities, items, fighting styles, solo mode, team mode and a lot more. Overall pretty fun to play with a group of friends. If you are planning on going just solo be ready to get killed until you get good. Very Easy to play but hard to master with many options which keep the game and replay value alive. Is it a game you can easily play 100 hours in? Yes but continuous 100 hours? Probably not more like several hours a day than take a break kinda game. But it is still very entertaining and almost every game is different I cannot wait to see what they add in the future and I will keep coming back.  Cons: Yes there are bots in the game but there are also people as well. Sometimes the bots can be very annoying especially when it feels like they are on your team and do not listen. However the bots still do a pretty decent job when fighting as it appears the difficulty goes up the closer to end game you get.   Also they do have micro-transactions but these are pretty much just cosmetic only so anyone complaining that this ruins the game is wrong. You can literally get any item in the game by playing for free. It will take you some time sure but think of it like Genshin Impact where it takes time to get gear, items etc. They also have a battle pass system that you can purchase to get more items etc faster if you want to. All the cosmetics you do buy are actually kind of nice and can be seen clearly in the game from weapon skins to how your character looks. Overall  one of the better games in terms of buying content etc it is actually worth it.  Overall this game is pretty fun and for 20 bucks honestly is a good deal. They have lots of players playing right now and as you rank up you will start fighting people who are really really good! So great game with friends and solo if that is your jam. Hope this helps with anyone on the fence. I would also just buy it and in the first two hours you don't like it than just return it overall its a win win for everyone.

As you progress through the levels, twelve in total you'll encounter new mechanics that will add more complexity and will require a faster reaction time as more things will keep you from keeping your plants alive. You are rated from 1 up to 3 star based on your performance on each level, and there is also achievement connected to each stage. You also have access to a journal which indicates the different needs of each plant that you discover and some information. You can customize your character and the controls. Your greenhouse will also get modified as you meet the level requirements. And it's free. Overall, it is a really pleasant management game, had a fun time playing it.

Après 43h de jeu, j'ai un terrible constat à faire, les développeurs n'avaient aucune imagination. On leur donne un univers riche et rempli de créatures magiques, il y a même un livre disponibles qui détaille les différentes créatures présentes dans cet univers mais tout ce qu'ils ont trouvé à faire, c'est du remplissage à coups d'araignées géantes... Elles sont partout, vous rentrez dans un tombeau pensant tomber sur des Inferis ? Non, c'est remplis d'araignée du sol au plafond. Elles doivent largement représentés plus de 50% des ennemis que l'on affronte dans ce jeu. Le bémol ? Les Acromentules n'ont été introduites à Poudlard que 50 ans plus tard par Hagrid, il n'y a aucun moment dans les livres ou les héros rencontrent des araignées géantes qui ne soient pas des Acromentules donc d'ou sortes toutes ces espèces que l'on rencontre et pourquoi il n'y a que ça ?  L'avantage, c'est que vu l'abattage général que fait notre protagoniste, c'est facile de justifier leur disparition vu qu'on ne combat que ça, on doit probablement avoir causer leur disparition. Le jeu reste bon malgré tout, on peut sentir l'amour qui a été mis dans le gameplay, il est très précis, les sorts sont super, il y a plein de combo de sort cachés à découvrir, les défis nous permettent d'en découvrir plein, c'est juste dommage que le même amour n'ait pas été offert au bestiaire du jeu. Le craft de potion, l'élevage d'animaux, l'amélioration de l'équipement sont des fonctionnalités super intéressante à découvrir seulement entaché par une difficulté au ras du sol (La, encore une fois, c'est un problème de bestiaire, pas de variété, pas de nouveaux monstres une fois passés les 10 premières heures, on roule sur le jeu car les ennemis sont toujours les mêmes...). Je peux pardonner ce qui manque parce que le studio manquait de moyen/expérience et que l'on peut vraiment sentir l'amour porté au gameplay mais un gameplay bon sans renouvellement des ennemis devient ennuyeux, une fois tout les sorts débloqués, il n'y a plus vraiment de plaisir à continuer car rien de nouveau ne se produira... Le vol sur balai est également décevant, il est trop rigide, il aurait beaucoup mieux de pouvoir incliner le balai dans la direction de notre choix et avoir un vrai vol libre plutôt qu'un vol ultra linéaire ou on gère l'altitude en montant/descendant avec une touche sans pouvoir faire de piqué. En réumé: Bon point : -Un gameplay vraiment agréable.  Mauvais points: -Mais qui devient lassant fautes d'ennemis variés -Bestiaire ridicule au delà du recyclage. (Fangieux, Inferi, sorcier, gobelin, troll et 50% d'araignées.) -Pas de coupe des 4 maisons (alors que c'est pas si compliqué à faire au fond.) -Pas de possibilités de déclencher des duels entre Elèves dans l'école (Sérieusement ?) -Pas de Quidditch (Bon, je peux pardonner) -Pas de tournoi des 3 sorciers (En pleine période ou le dernier avant Harry Potter avait eu lieu, sérieux !)

[code]For other game reviews, please [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/40640212/]follow us at What The Game?[/url][/code]  Dodgeball Academia is a game set in a world that revolves around - you guessed it, dodgeballs. The game features a single-player story mode wherein you will join Otto and train to become the ultimate dodgeball champion. Then there’s a versus mode, where you can sit back and play locally with your friends (or by yourself, no judging). This RPG game is giving me a lot of classic Pokémon vibes, from the transition music, the menu UI, some gameplay mechanics and more. And I am here for all of it!  Since there isn’t that much to go on about the versus mode, this review will specifically focus on the single-player story mode.  You will play as Otto, a transfer student in the academy, who aspires to be the best dodgeball player out there. The story unfolds like it’s some sort of a Saturday morning cartoon. Its cartoonish art style and the same time, combining a 2.5D world and 2D sprite sets this game apart distinctively. The story progresses somewhat linearly, having a main quest each day and a few optional quests in between. Its main quest dubbed as an ‘episode’ really makes this game feel like you’re watching a cartoon series.  The gameplay of dodgeball is very simple. Two teams are matched and the first team that gets wiped out, loses. If you are familiar with the game, then you had a nice childhood. But if not, don’t fret because the game did a nice job of introducing the rules to you. Your team may compose from one to three members, while the enemy team will range from one to six. You control one character or switch up to another on the fly during the matches.  Throughout the story mode, you will come across unique characters that will contribute to your story progression. With each character having different characteristics, they also come with different set of abilities; from counters, whether to dodge or jump, and balltimates (ultimate moves). As you progress through the story, you will be unlocking characters that will join your team. You can freely customize your party in the main menu.  There are two types of obtainable items in the game; (1) consumables that can heal/revive your party members or give a permanent stat boost, (2) equipment that will give you additional boosts in your stats if your characters have them equipped. Each character can only equip up to two items, so plan strategically. While for the consumables, it is worth taking note that each character also has preference. Meaning to say, some consumables will have a better effect to those who loves or likes the food as opposed to dislikes and allergic to it. Aside from using consumable items, you may also get your team healed up in an infirmary.  The core gameplay of dodgeball can get repetitive quite fast if you’re burning through this game quickly. Since all the main quests and optional quests will revert to you playing dodgeball. I highly suggest that play this game in short bursts to avoid the feeling of it becoming a chore. The game is fairly short, ranging from 10 to 15 hours of playtime to finish the story mode. So, there is no point of rushing this one, just take your time and let the game come to you.  With the positive notes out of the way, now it’s time to tackle some negative ones. First off, your other team members are pretty much useless. All their movements and actions will depend on the character that you’re using. It’s crazy seeing your enemy moving so independently and contributing to win the match. Your teammates will shadow you, mimicking your movements. It’s already hard enough to dodge volley of balls thrown at you, imagine having to that while minding your teammates position. And they are not contributing at all. I often feel like my other team members are only there just so I have a backup life just in case my character’s health depletes to zero.  Next is that rolling ball mode (sprinting). Since by default, your moving animation is already running, going from point A to point B can be hassle especially if it’s on the other side of the campus. Thus, they are introducing this rolling ball to somewhat kind of sprint. On paper, this shouldn’t be something negative, right? Wrong. Going into a roll feels like you don’t have any real directional control. You will bang keep banging into something and this will eventually annoy the hell out of you.  Overall, I do recommend this game to anyone who has an itch for a sports RPG. Its visuals and soundtrack make this game really stand out. Story-wise, it’s not that heavy and that’s fine for me. The core gameplay of dodgeball is solid especially with how they’ve added a cartoonish twist to it. The ability effects are amazing and satisfying to execute. And besides, there isn’t that many dodgeball games out there. So, grab a copy and start playing!

[b]Disappointment on the Track[/b]  Rating: ★☆☆☆☆  F1 Manager 2022 comes off the starting line with a sputter rather than a roar, failing to live up to the high-octane excitement and strategic depth fans of Formula 1 expect from a management simulator.  Despite the absence of microtransactions, which is commendable in today's gaming landscape, the game still fails to deliver a rewarding or enjoyable player experience. It seems that the potential excitement of managing a professional racing team has been lost in translation, as the mechanics and features feel shallow and unrefined.  Worse still, there is an apparent lack of ongoing commitment from the developers post-launch. Bugs and issues that should have been rectified continue to exist in the game. Feedback from the community goes unheard, and updates are scarce, leading to a stagnated game state that does nothing to improve the lacking player experience.  The lack of developer engagement and neglect of the game so soon after its release leaves a bitter taste. Without any signs of imminent improvement, it's challenging to foresee the game gaining traction or maintaining a dedicated player base. The developers need to reconsider their current stance and provide the necessary updates and fixes to retain their audience and draw new players.  All these factors culminate in a disappointing experience with F1 Manager 2022. The game's shortcomings overshadow the thrill of running an F1 team, reducing what could have been a deeply strategic and immersive experience into a lackluster affair.  The bottom line is this: If you're looking for a detailed and dynamic sports management game, F1 Manager 2022 in its current state is, unfortunately, a pitstop you might want to pass. The lack of developer support and refinement in the game mechanics make it a difficult title to recommend.

I have >400 hours on switch+epic version of this game. Not one to typically speedrun any game, but I liked this game enough that I decided to start speedrunning it (half that playtime is from speedrunning).  The other half the playtime is just playing casually, getting max% took some time, and it's pretty fun to clear levels on the switch when lazing around.  Common misconceptions that the game is: a) endless runner. it's not endless, there are levels, story, bosses and chapters just like in the first smb. b) randomly generated levels. The levels are not completely randomly generated, each level is made by piecing together handcrafted chunks.  The gameplay does not fit the mold of an autorunner, and the only element it shares with them is that you move forward without pressing anything. Most runners, like geometry dash, bit-trip runner series, the gameplay loop revolves around reacting to the stage, reacting to what's thrown at the player, often like a series of quick-time events or playing to a rhythm. While that still happens in SMBF, it is to a much lesser extent, here, the player is given control and the stage/game reacts to you. While the autorunning makes the gave less forgiving, as it's hard to recover from mistakes. Once you get used to the autorunning, it kind of takes a backseat, and it plays more like a platformer than a runner - as you're able to use dives and dashes to make adjustments to your movement rather than just having the fixed trajectory of your initial jump.   Getting S ranks is akin to going for SS in games like Dustforce, where you're trying to get a clean run throughout the entire level.  The game does suffer a little bit from telling the player what to do, especially in the later stages, where chunks can be pretty convoluted, it takes a bunch of death to parse the level and figure out where to go.

"기본적으로 만듦새도 괜찮고 재미도 있다. 근데 '압긍'일 정도인가? 라는 의문이 남는다.  이제는 2인 퍼즐이 그 자체만으로 신선함을 주는 시절은 지났다. 이 게임이 나올 당시에도 벌써 We were here 시리즈가 4개나 나오고, it takes two라는 걸출한 대작도 나왔다. 거슬러 올라가면 Portal2까지 포함할 수 있을거다. 그 외에도 훌륭한 작품은 많았다.  서로 시야를 공유하지 못하는 단절 상황에서, 대화만으로 소통하며 단서를 주고받아야 하는 게임성은 앞선 게임들과 동일하다.   근데 이 게임, 퍼즐의 수준이 너무나 얄팍하다.  힌트들은 조금만 살펴봐도 상대방이 읊는 것들을 어디에 넣어야할지 너무 분명하다.  한 예로, 상대방이 x1y3z2 라는 일련의 코드를 불러줬다. 그 말을 들은 나는 3차원 좌표를 통해 뭔가를 유추해야 할 줄 알았다. 그러나 상자를 살펴보던 나는 깜짝 놀랄 수밖에 없었다. 상자에는 x,y,z,1,2,3 단 6개의 버튼만 달린 입력 패널이 있었다. 내가 해야 할 일은 너무나 명확했다. 단지6가지 코드를 순서대로 입력하는 것 뿐이었다. 이 작업는 놀랍게도 여러번 반복된다.   이걸 퍼즐이라고 할 수 있을까? 받아쓰기가 이것보다 어려울거다. 과장을 좀 보태자면, 침팬지도 교육을 좀 받으면 사육사가 불러주는 6가지 버튼을 순서대로 누르는건 할 수 있지 않을까 싶을 정도다.  대부분의 퍼즐은 같은 방식으로 이루어진다. 단서를 불러주면, 그냥 1차원적으로 불러주는걸 누르면 된다. 이 게임에서 내가 할 고민은 딱 하나다. 전달받은 단서를 '어디'에 넣어야할까? 단서가 무엇을 의미하는지, 어떤 상징인지, 어느 관점에서 풀어야할지는 고민할 가치도 없다. 그냥 넣으면 그만이다.  원래부터 러스티레이크 시리즈는 내 기준에서 맛있는 퍼즐 게임은 아니었다. 사실 퍼즐보다는 포인트 앤 클릭을 통해 이 회사가 보여주는 세계와 서사를 탐구하는 것이 이 시리즈의 주된 즐거움일 것이다. 그렇게 보면 이 게임도 그냥 하던대로 잘 만든 게임이라고 볼 수 있다.  그럼에도 '2인코옵'과 '퍼즐'이라는 두가지 키워드가 유저에게 안겨주는 기대감은 꽤 크다. 그리고 그 기대감은 충족되지 않았다. 근데 왜 압긍인걸까? 그건 이 게임에 직관적으로 느낄 수 있는 '확실한 단점'이 없기 때문인 것 같다.   스팀 평가의 맹점은 긍정과 부정의 양자택일이라는 점이다.  10명이 한 게임을 평가할 때 모두 80점을 주면 이 게임은 80점짜리 쓸만한 범작인거다. 갓겜은 아닌 샘이다.  근데 80점을 긍정과 부정으로 보자면 분명 긍정일 것이다. 그럼 스팀에서는 아무 단점 없는 평범한 80점 짜리 게임이 긍정 비율 100퍼센트의 완벽한 갓겜으로 보이게된다.   그래서 나에게 이 게임의 가장 큰 단점은 ""압도적으로 긍정적""인 평가다.   아무리 생각해도 그 정도는 아니였거든."

This review is for the gamer who, like me, is an Elder Scrolls series fan but loathes other people and just wants to play this as a solo-player sequel to previous games. A bit of a niche market, but I can't be the only one -- so here goes.  Right up front I'll say that buying all of this game is wayyyy too expensive. That said, if you catch a sale at the right time you can get a big chunk of the content for about fifty bucks, and get enough of it that there's hundreds of hours of solo play. Vvardenfell from ES 3 and Skyrim from ES 5 are here and as you remember them, which is a big plus. It really is pretty fun seeing how history has continued to unfold in our old stomping grounds. Unfortunately Cyrodiil is a PvP zone so you probably won't want to put up with that just to see the central Empire again...  New regions are well-done, and we get some serious content for the Argonian and Khajit homelands that's pretty nice. Character creation is not as wide-open as earlier games, being character-class oriented, but it's OK. Graphics are not as nice as Skyrim with mods but are better than ES 4. The tradition of mini-games for lock-picking continues and has been extended to treaasure hunting too (though there's still basic treasure chest-seeking even if you don't buy the Greymoor DLC which has the full system). Some content -- multi-player dungeons, dolmen sites, world bosses -- is not solo-able, or at least not easily, but the quests and storylines are all pretty do-able.  In short, it's got some warts but you'll get your money's worth,

I think the thing that works incredibly well here is the gameplay loop between the fights and your investments in downtime between the fights. The ability to look at and choose between 3-4 upcoming fights (what they are, what rewards you can get, what bets you can place) at the same time as you shop for gear or consider training means you can strategize a fair amount going in to your next battle.   For example, if you have the option to take a many-on-one fight, it might not seem tempting since it pays less...but not only does it mean your odds of survival are better, it also means you can do things like skip a visit to the healer, or drop off some of your gear for repair, or even do some training (take a stamina hit) before that fight. But if you know you have a tougher fight ahead, maybe you have to invest your money in to just ensuring you win.  On top of that, your ability to spend resources outside the fights to advance your win conditions (ex- buying and donating equipment as a blacksmith aspirant) makes those choices even more complicated at times.  A very solid game already in Early Access.

The Dark Descent sets the bar really high... A Machine for Pigs walks face-first into that bar and kind of... flops.  If you've never played an Amnesia game before, this can be a good place to start. Voice acting is great, the scenery is pretty, and the sound design is effective. You get a good idea of what Frictional likes to set up with their storytelling and their puzzle-solving and progression... but if you've played other games in the franchise, this game just doesn't cut it.  Unlike The Dark Descent, there is no sanity system, no tinderboxes or oil (so no resource management), no real fear factor in the monster(s), and no drive to explore anything aside from aesthetics. It's a relatively simple game that borrows Frictional's concept, sort of like test-driving a car. It just so happens that this is a specific gameplay style that suits Frictional Games better than it does The Chinese Room, in my opinion.  That being said... it falls in line with games developed by The Chinese Room. Still a good game, just not for the Amnesia franchise!  If you're looking for an Amnesia game, do yourself a favour and play Amnesia: The Dark Descent; it's aged, but I would say it still holds its own.  If you're looking for a better Chinese Room-developed game, go for Dear Esther or Everybody's Gone to the Rapture. If you INSIST on playing this one... don't buy it at full price. Wait for it to go on sale.
